items.name: Pointer
items.docs:
A JSON Pointer, split on `/`: `/meta/y/z` is `["meta", "y", "z"]`,
and `""` is the whole row. SurrealDB does not escape a `/` or a `~`
in a field name (verified), so a part is the text between two `/`.
items.head: Pointer

items.name: pointer
items.docs: The parts of a pointer. A pointer other than `""` starts with `/`.

items.name: Op
items.signature: [Add(Pointer, Cbor.Value), Remove(Pointer), Replace(Pointer, Cbor.Value), Change(Pointer, TextPatch)]
items.docs:
One op of a patch, in the order of the patch. `Change` edits a
string in place with a text patch.
items.head: Op

items.name: op_of
items.signature: { op : Str, path : Str, value : Try(Cbor.Value, [Missing]) } -> Try(Op, [BadOp(Str)])
items.docs:
An op as the server sends it: `{ op, path, value }`. A `value` of
`NULL` is no key in the map, and is `Cbor.Value.Null` here.

items.name: path_of
items.docs: The pointer of an op.

items.name: apply
items.docs:
The value after the op. A part of a pointer is a key of a map, or an
index of an array; `-` is the end of an array for `Add`. `Add` puts
a value in an array before the index, and in a map sets the key.
`BadPath` is a pointer that the value does not have, and `Mismatch`
a text patch that does not fit the string.

items.name: Edit
items.docs: What an op does at the end of its pointer.
items.head: Edit

items.name: edit
items.signature: Cbor.Value, Pointer, Pointer, Edit -> Try(Cbor.Value, [BadPath(Pointer), Mismatch(U64)])
items.docs: The value with `edit` done at `rest`, the part of `path` that is left.

items.name: set_key
items.signature: List((Cbor.Value, Cbor.Value)), Str, Edit -> List((Cbor.Value, Cbor.Value))
items.docs:
The entries of a map with `key` set (`Insert`, `Put`) or removed
(`Drop`). A new key goes at the end.

items.name: at_index
items.signature: List(Cbor.Value), Str, Pointer, Edit -> Try(List(Cbor.Value), [BadPath(Pointer), Mismatch(U64)])
items.docs: The items of an array with the edit at the index `key`.

items.name: replace_at
items.docs: The items with the one at `i` replaced.

items.name: index_of
items.docs: An index below `size`, written in ASCII digits.

items.name: Part
items.docs:
One part of a hunk: text that both versions have, or that only the
new or only the old one has.
items.head: Part

items.name: Hunk
items.signature: { at : U64, before : U64, after : U64, parts : List(Part) }
items.docs:
One hunk of a text patch. `at` is where it starts in the text after
the hunks before it, in Unicode scalar values from 0. `before` and
`after` are the lengths of the old and the new text it covers.
items.head: Hunk

items.name: TextPatch
items.docs: A text patch: the hunks, in order.
items.head: TextPatch

items.name: parse
items.docs:
The hunks of a patch in the diff-match-patch text format: a header
`@@ -a,b +c,d @@` per hunk, then one line per part, which starts
with ` ` (keep), `-` (delete) or `+` (insert). A position counts
Unicode scalar values from 1, and a length of 0 counts from 0. A
length of 1 is left out of the header. The text of a part is UTF-8
with `%XX` escapes (`%0A` is a new line, `%25` is `%`).

items.name: apply
items.docs:
The text with each hunk applied, in order. The text must hold the
kept and the deleted parts of each hunk where the hunk starts:
`Mismatch(at)` gives that position when it does not.

items.name: read_line
items.docs: One line of a patch, added to the hunks read so far.

items.name: header
items.docs: The header `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` of a hunk, with no parts yet.

items.name: range
items.docs:
`a,b` as a start from 0 and a length: `a` alone has length 1, and a
length of 0 has its start from 0 already.

items.name: digits
items.docs: A number of ASCII digits only.

items.name: checked
items.docs: A hunk whose parts have the lengths of its header.

items.name: old_text
items.docs: The scalars a hunk covers in the old text: what it keeps and deletes.

items.name: new_text
items.docs: The scalars a hunk gives in the new text: what it keeps and inserts.

items.name: scalars
items.docs:
The UTF-8 bytes of each Unicode scalar value of a text: a scalar
starts at each byte that is not `10xxxxxx`.

items.name: apply_hunk
items.docs: One hunk applied to the scalars of the text.

items.name: unescape
items.docs: The text of a part: `%XX` is the byte `XX`, and the bytes are UTF-8.

items.name: State
items.docs: What the derived encoder threads through: the values built so far.
items.head: State

items.name: Item
items.docs:
One value on the stack. `Fields` is a record, and only `encode_record`
pushes it: the encoder of a record type, or of a nominal of the app over
a record. So the type of a union payload picks its form (`tagged`), not
the shape of its value.
items.head: Item

items.name: Format
items.docs:
The format the encoder is derived against. `U64`, `I128` and `U128`
have no method here on purpose: a row that holds one does not type-check
where it is written, because SurrealDB's `int` is 64-bit signed.
items.head: Format

items.name: encode_id
items.docs:
A record id, written by the hand-written encoders of `Surreal.Id`
and `Surreal.Link`.

items.name: encode_ref
items.docs:
A record id with a key of any value, written by the encoder of
`Surreal.Ref`.

items.name: encode_datetime
items.docs: A datetime, written by the encoder of `Surreal.Datetime`.

items.name: encode_geometry
items.docs:
A geometry as its GeoJSON object, written by the encoders of the
geometry types of `Surreal`. SurrealDB reads the object as a geometry.

items.name: encode_record
items.signature: Encode.State, U64, (Encode.State, (Encode.State, Str, (Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])
items.docs:
Each field pushes its name, then its value. A field that is absent
pushes nothing, so the key is left out.

items.name: encode_list
items.signature: Encode.State, U64, (Encode.State, (Encode.State, (Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])

items.name: encode_tag
items.signature: Encode.State, Str, U64, (Encode.State, (Encode.State, (Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])) -> Try(Encode.State, [])
items.docs:
The union payload rule: no payload is the bare tag
name, a record payload is spread next to `kind`, one other payload
is `value`, several are the array `value`. A record is a payload
that `encode_record` wrote (`Item`).

items.name: Bind
items.docs:
The format a captured value is bound in where its type may hold an
opaque type of another package (`Code.Binds`, `Surreal.select_where_with`).
The compiler runs the value's own `encoder_for` against it while the
program runs and hands the bytes to the translator, which reads them
back as the `Ql.Value` that `Encode.Format` gives for the same calls
(`Encode.bound`). Each value is a kind byte, then its contents: a text
is its byte count (8 bytes, big-endian) and its bytes, an integer 8
bytes, a `Dec` its attos in 16, a float its bits in 8, and a record, a
list and a tag hold their members up to a `0`.
items.head: Bind

items.name: encode_record
items.signature: List(U8), U64, (List(U8), (List(U8), Str, (List(U8) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])
items.docs:
Each field is a `7`, its name, then its value. A field that is
absent writes nothing, so the key is left out.

items.name: encode_list
items.signature: List(U8), U64, (List(U8), (List(U8), (List(U8) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])

items.name: encode_tag
items.signature: List(U8), Str, U64, (List(U8), (List(U8), (List(U8) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])) -> Try(List(U8), [])

items.name: big_endian
items.docs: The low `width` bytes of `bits`, the most significant first.

items.name: bound
items.docs: The value of the bytes `Bind` wrote for one captured value.

items.name: read_item
items.docs: The item that starts at `at`, and where the next one starts.

items.name: read_fields
items.signature: List(U8), U64, List({ name : Str, value : Ql.Value }) -> Try((List({ name : Str, value : Ql.Value }), U64), [BadBytes])

items.name: read_bits
items.docs: The `width` bytes at `at`, big-endian.

items.name: value_of
items.signature: a -> Try(Ql.Value, Ql.Error) where [a.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (a, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, []))]
items.docs: Encode a value the way a row is written.

items.name: fold_above
items.docs: The stack above `base` becomes one value on top of what was below.

items.name: pair_up
items.signature: List(Encode.Item), List({ name : Str, value : Ql.Value }) -> List({ name : Str, value : Ql.Value })
items.docs: Names and values alternate on the stack, as `encode_record` pushed them.

items.name: value
items.docs: The value of an item: a record is an object.

items.name: tagged
items.docs:
One union value from its tag and the payloads the arm carried. Only a
record payload is spread next to `kind`. A geometry is an object too,
but its type is not a record, so it is `value`, as the schema and the
reader have it.

items.name: Row
items.signature: { id : Str, qty : I64, price : Dec, ratio : F64, ok : Bool, tags : List(Str), note ?: Str, pay : [Cash, Card({ last4 : Str }), Check(I64), Wire(Str, I64)] }
items.head: Row

items.name: Auth
items.signature: { who : [Basic({ user : Str, pass : Str }), Bearer(Str), Anonymous], scope : [Scope({ ns : Str, db : Str }), FromToken] }
items.docs:
Who a post is from (`who`), and its namespace and database
(`scope`). `Basic` is a system user. `Bearer` is the token of a
record user (`signup`, `signin`) or of `authenticate`. `Anonymous`
is a post before a signup or a signin, and after `invalidate`. A
token holds its namespace and database, so a session of a token
alone sends none (`FromToken`): SurrealDB 3.3.4 runs a post with a
`Bearer` token and no `surreal-ns` in the token's (verified).
items.head: Auth

items.name: Post
items.signature: { uri : Str, headers : List({ name : Str, value : Str }), body : List(U8) }
items.docs: One post, as the platform sends it.
items.head: Post

items.name: post
items.docs:
The post of one RPC message to `url`, the base of the server, such
as `http://127.0.0.1:8000`: CBOR both ways, the authentication of
`auth`, and its namespace and database.

items.name: reply
items.signature: { status : U16, body : List(U8) } -> Try(List(U8), [Refused({ status : U16, message : Str })])
items.docs:
The RPC reply in a response. SurrealDB answers a request with status
200, also a request whose method or statement fails: the message
holds that error. Any other status is the server refusing the post,
such as 401 for a password that does not verify, with a text body:
the status, and the text, or `HTTP <status>` when there is none.

items.name: Error
items.signature: [Unsupported(Str), BadSchema(Str), Decode({ path : Str, message : Str }), Wire(Str), Server(ServerError), Aborted({ at : U64, error : ServerError }), Transport(Str), WebSocket([Closed(Ws.Closure), Closing, Adapter(Str)])]
items.docs:
Why a reified function is not SurrealQL, or a schema is not one
SurrealDB can create. Every rejection names the construct. A live
session adds six: `Decode` for a value of the server that does not
fit the Roc type it is read as, with the path to it when the reader
names one (`result.row.temp_c`, else empty), `Wire` for bytes from
the server that are not what the protocol says, `Server` for a
request or a statement that the server refused, by its kind,
`Aborted` for a transaction that a statement failed, `Transport`
for a post over HTTP that the platform could not do, and
`WebSocket` for an error of the WebSocket adapter (roc-websocket's
`Ws.Error`): the connection ended (`Closed`, with how), it is
closing (`Closing`), or a tag of the adapter, as `Str.inspect`
writes it (`Adapter`, such as `Tcp(TimedOut)` or `Refused("..")`).
`at` of `Aborted` is the place of the prepared statement that
failed it (`Transaction.then`): 0 for the first, and the count of
them for the `COMMIT`, such as a `Conflict`. Every other statement
of the transaction is rolled back, or did not run.
items.head: Error

items.name: ServerError
items.signature:
[
		Exists({ what : Str, name : Str, message : Str }),
		NotFound({ what : Str, name : Str, message : Str }),
		Unique({ table : Str, index : Str, fields : List(Str), value : Str, record : Str, message : Str }),
		Index({ index : Str, value : Str, record : Str, message : Str }),
		Assert({ table : Str, field : Str, record : Str, value : Str, condition : Str, message : Str }),
		Type({ table : Str, field : Str, record : Str, expected : Str, found : Str, message : Str }),
		Check({ table : Str, name : Str, message : Str }),
		Referenced({ record : Str, by : Str, message : Str }),
		Denied(Str),
		Parse(Str),
		Invalid(Str),
		Conflict(Str),
		Timeout(Str),
		Thrown({ text : Str, message : Str }),
		Other({ kind : Str, message : Str }),
	]
items.docs:
Why the server refused a request or a statement: the `kind` of its
error, and for the kind `Internal`, what its message says when the
message has the form SurrealDB 3.3.4 writes. Each keeps the message.

| Tag | The server's error |
| --- | --- |
| `Exists` | `AlreadyExists`: `what` is the details' kind (`Record`, `Table`, ..), `name` the record id or the name |
| `NotFound` | `NotFound`, as `Exists`: a table, a record, a method |
| `Unique` | A unique index of the schema the session knows (`Session.knowing`) already holds the value: its table and fields (SurrealQL paths) |
| `Index` | The same for an index the session does not know |
| `Assert` | A field's `ASSERT` fails: the field, the record, the value and the condition |
| `Type` | A value does not fit the field's `TYPE` |
| `Check` | A `.check(name, ..)` of the schema, which is an event, fails |
| `Referenced` | A delete of a record that a link with `Reject` points at: `by` is the linking record (a root link) or `table.path` (a nested link) |
| `Denied` | `NotAllowed`, a post that HTTP refuses with 401 or 403, or a signup, a signin or a token that the server refuses (`Session.open!`) |
| `Parse` | `Validation` whose message is a parse error |
| `Invalid` | Any other `Validation`, such as a protected variable |
| `Conflict` | `Query` with `TransactionConflict`: the transaction can be retried |
| `Timeout` | `Query` with `TimedOut` |
| `Thrown` | `Thrown`: a `THROW`, with its text |
| `Other` | Any other kind, or a message of another form |
items.head: ServerError

items.name: message
items.docs: The server's message, as it sent it.

items.name: Value
items.signature:
[
		None,
		Bool(Bool),
		Int(I64),
		Float(F64),
		Decimal(Dec),
		Str(Str),
		Datetime(Str),
		Record({ table : Str, key : Str }),
		Ref({ table : Str, key : Value }),
		Array(List(Value)),
		Object(List({ name : Str, value : Value })),
	]
items.docs:
One SurrealQL value, as a parameter, a seed or a default. `Float` and
`Decimal` stay apart because SurrealDB keeps them apart. `Record` is a
record id with a text key, and `Ref` one with a key of any value, such
as the array of a time series key.
items.head: Value

items.name: literal
items.docs: The value as source text: `'it\'s'`, `20dec`, `customer:⟨ada⟩`, `{ a: 1 }`.

items.name: float
items.docs:
A float with the `f` suffix, so a whole number stays a float. SurrealQL
spells the two non-finite values `NaN` and `Infinity`.

items.name: quote
items.docs: A string literal in single quotes.

items.name: ident
items.docs:
A table or field name, bare when SurrealQL reads it as a name and in
angle brackets otherwise (`⟨x y⟩`, `⟨select⟩`).

items.name: member
items.docs:
A name after a dot or an object key. Words such as `value` and `select`
are fine there (verified), so only a name that is not plain is bracketed.

items.name: record_id
items.docs:
A record id. The key is always bracketed, so any key is one token:
`customer:⟨o'neil⟩`, `customer:⟨x y⟩`.

items.name: record_ref
items.docs:
A record id with a key of any value: `t:⟨key⟩` for a text key, as
`record_id`, and `t:[..]` for an array key, the key of a time series.

items.name: keywords
items.docs:
Names SurrealQL does not accept bare as a table or a field. Found by
running each candidate word against SurrealDB 3.3.4.

items.name: is_plain
items.docs: A name made of lower case letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit.

items.name: escape
items.docs:
Text as it goes between quotes: `\`, the quote, and control characters
are escaped. Inside angle brackets, `⟩` is escaped too.

items.name: Uuid
items.docs:
The uuid of a live query: CBOR tag 37 and a byte string of 16 bytes.
SurrealDB gives one for each `LIVE SELECT`, and puts it in each
notice of that query.
items.head: Uuid

items.name: from_bytes
items.docs: The uuid of these 16 bytes.

items.name: to_str
items.docs: The text form: `8-4-4-4-12` hex digits.

items.name: parser_for
items.signature: Cbor -> (Cbor.State -> Try({ value : Uuid, rest : Cbor.State }, [InvalidCbor(U64)]))

items.name: signin
items.signature: U64, { user : Str, pass : Str } -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List({ user : Str, pass : Str }) }
items.docs: `signin` as a system user of the server.

items.name: access
items.signature: U64, Str, { ns : Str, db : Str, access : Str }, List((Cbor.Value, Cbor.Value)) -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List(Cbor.Value) }
items.docs:
`signup` or `signin` (`method`) of a record user: one map of the
namespace, the database, the access method (`ac`) and the variables
of its `SIGNUP` or `SIGNIN` query. The reply is the token.

items.name: authenticate
items.signature: U64, Str -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List(Str) }
items.docs: `authenticate`: the session is the user of a token.

items.name: invalidate
items.signature: U64 -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List(Str) }
items.docs: `invalidate`: the session is no one.

items.name: use_db
items.signature: U64, Str, Str -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List(Str) }
items.docs: `use`: the namespace and the database of the session.

items.name: query
items.signature: U64, Str -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List(Str) }
items.docs: `query`: one text of statements, such as `Watch.request`.

items.name: kill
items.signature: U64, Uuid -> { id : U64, method : Str, params : List(Uuid) }
items.docs: `kill`: the end of a live query. SurrealDB sends `KILLED` for it.

items.name: Policy
items.docs: What a delete does to the rows that link to the deleted row.
items.head: Policy

items.name: Rule
items.signature:
[
		Assert({ path : Str, cond : Str }),
		Check({ name : Str, cond : Str }),
		Index({ paths : List(Str), unique : Bool }),
		SearchIndex({ path : Str, kind : Str, spec : Str, analyzers : List(Str) }),
		Default({ path : Str, value : Str }),
		Computed({ path : Str, expr : Str }),
		Readonly(Str),
		Comment({ path : Str, text : Str }),
		OnDelete({ table : Str, policy : Schema.Policy }),
		OnDeleteAt({ path : Str, policy : Schema.Policy }),
		Changefeed(U64),
		Permit({ actions : List(Schema.Action), grant : Schema.Grant }),
		PermitField({ path : Str, actions : List(Schema.Action), grant : Schema.Grant }),
	]
items.docs:
One clause of the builder, translated. Paths are spelled as a field
definition names them (`items[*].qty`). Conditions are over `$value`,
a row check is over `$after`, a computed value is over `$this`.
items.head: Rule

items.name: Action
items.docs:
What a permission is for: a statement of a record user that reads
or writes the table or the field.
items.head: Action

items.name: Grant
items.docs:
A permission: the rows that the condition keeps (`WHERE`, over the
row, which may read the session: `$auth.id`), every row, or none.
items.head: Grant

items.name: Defined
items.signature:
[
		Table({ source : Types.Source, rules : List(Schema.Rule), problems : List(Ql.Error) }),
		Function(Try(List(Schema.Function), Ql.Error)),
		Read({ name : Str, row_ty : Code.Ty }),
		Access(Try(Str, Ql.Error)),
		Analyzer({ name : Str, line : Str }),
	]
items.docs:
A finished table definition, the database functions of one
`Surreal.function`, or a read row of a table, which writes no
statement and is checked against the stored row: what
`Surreal.schema` takes.
items.head: Defined

items.name: Function
items.signature: { name : Str, params : List(Code.Ty), result : Code.Ty, body : Str }
items.docs:
A database function, translated: `$a1`, `$a2`, .. have the types of
`params`, and `body` is the value it returns.
items.head: Function

items.name: analyzer
items.docs:
`DEFINE ANALYZER`, which a full-text index names: a statement of
the database, before every table.

items.name: search_index
items.signature: Str, Str, Str, List(Str) -> Try(List(Schema.Rule), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A full-text or a vector index on the field at `path`: `kind` names
it, `spec` is what follows `FIELDS path` (`FULLTEXT ANALYZER a BM25
HIGHLIGHTS`, `HNSW DIMENSION 3 DIST COSINE TYPE F64`), and
`analyzers` the analyzer it names, which the schema must define.

items.name: access
items.signature: { name : Str, table : Str, content : Try(Str, Ql.Error), cond : Try(Str, Ql.Error), token : Try(U64, [Unset]), session : Try(U64, [Unset]) } -> Schema.Defined
items.docs:
`DEFINE ACCESS name ON DATABASE TYPE RECORD`: a signup is a
`CREATE` of the content, a signin a `SELECT` of the row that the
condition keeps, each over the variables of the RPC as `$name`.
The durations are nanoseconds; one that is not given is
SurrealDB's default (a token of 1 hour, a session with no end).

items.name: tables
items.docs:
The tables of the definitions, where a link finds its table: each
stored row, and each read row with the name of its table.

items.name: Hop
items.docs:
One step to a link: a field, each element of a list, the arm of a
union (the value there is that arm), or one item of an array.
items.head: Hop

items.name: Site
items.signature: { hops : List(Schema.Hop), target : Code.Ty, optional : Bool }
items.docs:
A `Link` or `Id` in a row. A list of links ends in `Each`. `optional`
is True when the link's own field is `?:`.
items.head: Site

items.name: check
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Types.Source, Str, Code.Graph -> Try(List(Schema.Rule), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A row check, placed by one rule: when it reads only one top-level
field, it is that field's `ASSERT`; when it reads more, it is an event
over `$after`; when it reads none, it is an error. `extensions` give
the forms of the calls of each clause here (`Translate.form`).

items.name: permit
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Types.Source, List(Schema.Action), [Where(Code.Graph), Full, No] -> Try(List(Schema.Rule), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A permission of the table for `actions`: the condition over the
row, a `filter`'s (`Translate.table_row`), or `FULL` or `NONE`.

items.name: permit_field
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Types.Source, Code.Graph, List(Schema.Action), [Where(Code.Graph), Full, No] -> Try(List(Schema.Rule), Ql.Error)
items.docs: A permission of the field at a path for `actions`, as `permit`.

items.name: grant
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Types.Source, [Where(Code.Graph), Full, No] -> Try(Schema.Grant, Ql.Error)

items.name: permissions
items.signature: Str, List({ actions : List(Schema.Action), grant : Schema.Grant }), Bool -> Try(Str, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
`PERMISSIONS FOR select WHERE .., FOR create, update FULL`: one
`FOR` for each permission, in the order given. Each action is in
one at most. A table names the actions that no permission names
`NONE`, which is SurrealDB's default for a table; a field leaves
them out, and SurrealDB's default for a field is `FULL`.

items.name: placed
items.signature: List(Translate.Extension), Code.Graph, List(Types.Field) -> [NoField, OnField({ name : Str, cond : Str }), Several]
items.docs:
Where a predicate over a record goes. It is evaluated with the record
holding one field at a time, bound to `$value`: it evaluates exactly
when it reads nothing outside that field.

items.name: assert

The schema script: every `DEFINE FUNCTION`, then every `DEFINE ANALYZER`, then every `DEFINE TABLE`,
then every view, then every field, then the indexes, the row-check
events, the delete events and the access methods, so that no statement names a function or
a table defined later. A view that calls a function needs it defined
first (verified).

items.docs:
One `DEFINE FUNCTION` for each name. A function that two
`Surreal.function` entries reach is written once; two different bodies
with one name are a `BadSchema`.

items.docs: `DEFINE FUNCTION OVERWRITE fn::name($a1: T1, ..) -> R { RETURN body };`

items.docs: Each full-text index of a table names an analyzer of the schema.

a default: `.default_by(|r| r.id, |_| Surreal.Rand.ulid())` is
`DEFINE FIELD id .. TYPE string DEFAULT rand::ulid()`, and a create
with no key gets that key (`Table.create_new`). A key with no
default has no definition, and SurrealDB makes a random key.

items.docs:
A view: `DEFINE TABLE .. AS SELECT ..`. SurrealDB fills it from its
query, so it has no field definitions, and it takes no rule: a view is
read-only.

items.docs: The name of the event of `Def.check`.

items.signature: { index : Str, table : Str, fields : List(Str) }
items.docs: A unique index that the schema defines: its name, table and paths.
items.head: Known

items.name: unique_indexes
items.docs:
The unique indexes of the definitions, which `Session.knowing`
keeps so that a violation of one names its fields.

items.name: violation
items.docs:
An error of the kind `Internal`, read from its message where it has
a form that SurrealDB 3.3.4 writes for a constraint (verified):

| Message | Tag |
| --- | --- |
| ``Database index `i` already contains v, with record `r` `` | `Unique` for a known index, else `Index` |
| ``Found v for field `f`, with record `r`, but field must conform to: c`` | `Assert` |
| ``Couldn't coerce value for field `f` of `r`: Expected `t` but found `v` `` | `Type` |
| ``Cannot delete `r` as it is referenced by `b` with an ON DELETE REJECT clause`` | `Referenced` (a root link) |
| ``Error while processing event e: An error occurred: t`` | `Check` when `e` and `t` are those of a `Def.check`; `Referenced` when `e` is the delete event of a nested link; else `Thrown` |
| ``Error while processing event e: m`` | What `m` is |

Any other message is `Other`. A record id is as the server writes
it, `vet:a` or `` `my t`:k ``; the table is the part before `:`.

items.name: thrown_in
items.docs:
The text that an event threw: a `Def.check` throws `table: name`
from the event `table_check_<name>`, and the delete event of a
nested link `record is referenced by table.path`.

items.name: table_of
items.docs:
The table of a record id as the server writes it: `vet` of `vet:a`,
`my t` of `` `my t`:k ``.

items.name: no_cycle
items.signature: List({ source : Types.Source, rules : List(Schema.Rule), problems : List(Ql.Error) }), Types.Registry -> Try({}, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
Rows are written one at a time and each link must exist, so a cycle of
required root links can never be filled.

items.head: Edge

What the translator does not look inside (see `cut`): every type
below with a method that takes `Code` names this list.

items.docs:
Why a statement is not built or does not run, one type for every
call (see `Ql.Error`): `Unsupported` and `BadSchema` when the
program builds it, then `Transport`, `Wire`, `Server` and `Decode`
when a session runs it.
items.head: Error

items.docs:
Why the server refused a request or a statement, by the kind of its
error (see `Ql.ServerError`).
items.head: ServerError

items.name: Id
items.docs:
A typed record id: `customer:⟨ada⟩`. The type parameter `row` ties the
id to its row type: no value holds it, and the type checker keeps an
`Id(Customer)` from an `Id(Product)`. The reifier gives it as the
type argument of the `Named` (`Types.row_of`), so a captured id holds
only its table and key.
items.head: Id(row)

items.name: is_eq
items.docs: Equal when the table and the key are equal.

items.name: key
items.docs: The key, without the table: `record::id(id)` in a clause.

items.name: Created
items.docs:
A row that `Table.create_new` or `Table.insert_new` made, with the
key that the server gave it: its `Id`, and its other fields as
stored. `new` is the row without its `id`, so a `Created(Customer,
{ name : Str })` reads `made.id.key()` and `made.fields.name`, and
`customers.link(made.id.key())` links to it.
items.head: Created(row, new)

items.name: Link
items.docs:
A stored link. `fetched` holds the row when the application has it (seed
data, a row read back). In a clause, `get` is a traversal: `customer.name`.
items.head: Link(row)

items.name: get
items.docs:
The row. A link that was not fetched has none, and this crashes: the
row lives in the database, so only a clause can read through it.

items.name: id
items.docs:
The record id the link holds: the id itself in a clause. In a clause
the field `link.id` is the same. The field `fetched` has no meaning
in the database, so a clause that reads it is refused.

items.name: is_eq
items.docs: Equal when the ids are equal.

items.name: parser_for
items.signature: Cbor -> (Cbor.State -> Try({ value : Link(row), rest : Cbor.State }, [InvalidCbor(U64)]))
items.docs: A link from the server: its record id. The row is not fetched.

items.name: Linked
items.docs:
A read view of a link: the linked row, read as a field of this row,
so `p.owner.name` is the traversal `owner.name` with no `.get()`. It
is for reads only. A row that holds one has no encoder, so a write of
it is a type error, and the stored row of its table holds a `Link`
at the same place (`Table.define_read` checks it). The linked row is
an alias of a record or a nominal over one, also a row that links to
its own table (`Linked(Owner)` with `referred_by ?: Link(Owner)`), or a
read row. It finds its table by its row, the type argument, as a `Link`.
items.head: Linked(row)

items.name: linked
items.docs: A `Linked` that holds its row: a Roc value of a read view.

items.name: Out
items.docs:
The edges that leave the row, in a field of a read view that has the
name of the edge table: `treats : Surreal.Out(Treats)` is `->treats`.
It is not stored, and `Table.define_read` checks that the edge table
starts at this table.
items.head: Out(edge)

items.name: list
items.docs: The edges: `v.treats.list().len()` is `->treats.len()`.

items.name: In
items.docs:
The edges that end at the row, in a field of a read view that has the
name of the edge table: `treats : Surreal.In(Treats)` is `<-treats`.
`Table.define_read` checks that the edge table ends at this table.
items.head: In(edge)

items.name: list
items.docs: The edges: `p.treats.list().len()` is `<-treats.len()`.

items.name: Datetime
items.docs:
A SurrealDB `datetime`, held as UTC ISO 8601 with a `Z`

times are equal strings. Make one with `datetime`.
items.head: Datetime

items.name: is_lt
items.docs:

the `Z` kept, `...59Z` would sort after `...59.5Z`.

items.name: datetime
items.docs:
A datetime from `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, an optional fraction of up to
nine digits, and `Z`. Other offsets are refused: the order of the text
is the order of the time only in UTC.

series is an `Id`, a `Str`, an integer, or a record of them for a key

`TimeKey` is a time series, and `Query.between` reads one range of it.

time. SurrealDB refuses a time outside the nanoseconds of an `I64`

a span above `I64.highest` nanoseconds, so these stop the program.

items.name: hour
items.docs: `time::hour`: 0 to 23.

items.name: minute
items.docs: `time::minute`: 0 to 59.

items.name: second
items.docs: `time::second`: 0 to 59, without the fraction.

items.name: digits
items.docs: The number in `count` digits of the text of a datetime, from byte `start`.

items.name: mean
items.docs: `math::mean`. A list with no value has no mean: the result is not a number.

items.name: median
items.docs: `math::median`. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: stddev
items.docs: `math::stddev`: the sample deviation. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: variance
items.docs: `math::variance`: the sample variance. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: percentile
items.docs: `math::percentile`: a value of the list, with the percentage 0 to 100, interpolated. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: uuid
items.docs: `rand::uuid`, as text.

items.name: ulid
items.docs: `rand::ulid`: 26 characters that sort by time.

items.name: int
items.docs: `rand::int`: a whole number from the first to the second, both included.

items.name: area
items.docs: `geo::area`: the area on the earth in square metres. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: bearing
items.docs: `geo::bearing`: the direction from the first point to the second, in degrees. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: centroid
items.docs: `geo::centroid`: the centre of the geometry. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: distance
items.docs: `geo::distance`: the distance on the earth in metres. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: hash_encode
items.docs:
`geo::hash::encode`: the geohash of the point in 1 to 12 characters.
SurrealDB refuses another length with an error. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: hash_decode
items.docs: `geo::hash::decode`: the centre of the cell of a geohash. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: is_valid
items.docs:
`geo::is_valid`: every longitude is from -180 to 180 and every
latitude from -90 to 90. A NaN is not. SurrealDB stores a point out
of range, so a field of a geometry type asserts this.

items.name: contains
items.docs: `a CONTAINS b`: the first geometry holds the second. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: inside
items.docs: `a INSIDE b`: the second geometry holds the first. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: outside
items.docs: `a OUTSIDE b`: the geometries have no point in common. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: intersects
items.docs: `a INTERSECTS b`: the geometries have a point in common. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: Tokenizer
items.docs:
A tokenizer of an analyzer. `Blank` splits a text at white space,
`Class` where the class of a character changes (a letter, a digit,
white space, anything else), `Camel` before an upper-case letter
that follows a lower-case one, and `Punct` at punctuation, which
it keeps as tokens.
items.head: Tokenizer

items.name: TokenFilter
items.signature: [Lowercase, Uppercase, Ascii, Snowball(Str), EdgeNgram(U8, U8), Ngram(U8, U8)]
items.docs:
A filter of the tokens of an analyzer, in the order given:
`Snowball("english")` is the stem of a word, `EdgeNgram(1, 3)` its
first one to three characters.
items.head: TokenFilter

items.name: Analyzer
items.signature: { name : Str, tokenizers : List(Tokenizer), filters : List(TokenFilter) }
items.docs:
An analyzer of the database, `DEFINE ANALYZER`: how a full-text
index (`Table.text_index`) and a search (`Query.search`) cut a text
into terms. Give `define()` to `schema`.

`clinical = Surreal.analyzer("clinical", [Class], [Lowercase])`
items.head: Analyzer

items.name: define
items.docs: `DEFINE ANALYZER OVERWRITE name TOKENIZERS .. FILTERS ..;`

items.name: tokens
items.docs:
The terms of a text, as `search::analyze` gives them. The Roc
meaning covers the tokenizers `Blank` and `Class` and the filters
`Lowercase` and `Uppercase`, over ASCII text, where it is the
server's (verified on 3.3.4). Another analyzer, or a text with a
character outside ASCII, runs in the database only: the call
stops the program.

items.name: matches
items.docs:
Whether a full-text search over this analyzer keeps the text: the
query has a term, and the text has every term of it, as
`text @@ query` (verified on 3.3.4: a query of no term, such as
`''`, keeps no row, and a query of two terms keeps the rows that
have both). The Roc meaning of `Query.search`, under the rule of
`tokens`.

items.name: analyzer
items.docs: An analyzer of this name, with its tokenizers and filters.

items.name: FullText
items.signature: { table : Str, path : Try(Str, Error), analyzer : Analyzer }
items.docs:
A full-text index of a `Str` field of a table, over an analyzer
(`Table.text_index`): the definition (`Def.text_index`) and the
searches (`Query.search`) take the same value.
items.head: FullText(row)

items.name: Distance
items.docs: How a vector index measures the distance of two vectors.
items.head: Distance

items.name: VectorIndex
items.signature: { table : Str, path : Try(Str, Error), dimension : U64, distance : Distance, element : Try(Str, Error) }
items.docs:
A vector index of a `List(F64)` or `List(F32)` field of a table
(`Table.vector_index`), HNSW: the definition (`Def.vector_index`)
and the searches (`Query.nearest`) take the same value, so a probe
of another dimension is refused when the query is built.
items.head: VectorIndex(row)

items.name: Knn
items.docs:
The rows of `Query.nearest`: the `k` nearest by the distance of
the index, `<|k,ef|>` through the HNSW graph with `ef` candidates,
which may miss a row, or `<|k,DISTANCE|>`, every row measured.
items.head: Knn

items.name: score
items.docs:
`search::score(1)`: the BM25 score of the row for the terms of
the search. A term that half the rows or more have adds 0.

items.name: highlight
items.docs:
`search::highlight(before, after, 1)`: the text with each term
of the search between `before` and `after`.

items.name: offsets
items.signature: Hit -> List({ start : I64, end : I64 })
items.docs:
`search::offsets(1)`: where each term of the search is in the
text, from `start` to `end`, `end` left out.

items.name: distance
items.docs:
`vector::distance::knn()`: the distance of the row from the
probe, by the distance of the index. Through the HNSW graph it
is computed on the index's own copy of the vector (`TYPE F32`
rounds it), so it has no Roc meaning; measure the row with
`Vector` for one.

items.name: similarity_cosine
items.docs:
`vector::similarity::cosine`: the dot product over the product of
the magnitudes. A zero vector gives `NaN`.

items.name: distance_euclidean
items.docs: `vector::distance::euclidean`.

items.name: distance_manhattan
items.docs: `vector::distance::manhattan`: the sum of the differences.

items.name: distance_chebyshev
items.docs: `vector::distance::chebyshev`: the largest difference.

items.name: dot
items.docs: `vector::dot`.

items.name: magnitude
items.docs: `vector::magnitude`: the length of the vector.

items.name: DbFn
items.docs:
A Roc function that the database also holds, as `fn::name`. Make it a
top-level constant with `db_fn`, and give it to `schema` with `function`.
A call in a clause is `fn::name(..)`, and a call in Roc runs `run`.
items.head: DbFn(f)

items.name: call1
items.docs: `fn::name(a)`.

items.name: call2
items.signature: DbFn((a, b -> r)), a, b -> r
items.docs: `fn::name(a, b)`.

items.name: call3
items.signature: DbFn((a, b, c -> r)), a, b, c -> r
items.docs: `fn::name(a, b, c)`.

items.name: db_fn
items.docs:
A database function named `fn::name`. `name` is `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`, and
`run` is a top-level function:

fever_fn : Surreal.DbFn((Dec, I64 -> Bool))
fever_fn = Surreal.db_fn("fever", fever)

items.name: function
items.docs:
The `DEFINE FUNCTION` of a database function and of each database
function its body calls, for `schema`: `Surreal.function(|_| fever_fn)`.

items.name: TableKind
items.signature: [Normal, Relation({ from : Str, to : Str }), View]
items.docs:
What a table is: a normal table, an edge table with the names of the
tables its ends point at, or a view.
items.head: TableKind

items.name: Table
items.docs:
A table whose rows are `row`. It holds the name and the kind, and no
`Code` value, so a clause can read it: `visits.rows()`,
`vets.id("ruth")`. The row type comes from `define()`, where
`Types` reads the schema off it.
items.head: Table(row)

items.name: id
items.docs:
The id of a row of this table. In a clause it is the record id:
`vets.id("ruth")` is `vet:⟨ruth⟩`.

items.name: at
items.docs:
The row with this key, to start a query from: `FROM vet:⟨tia⟩`.
SurrealDB reads the one record, where a filter on the key
reads the table (see `Translate.key_compare`).
`Selected.prepare_one` reads the result as the row or
`NotFound`. The key is an escaped record id, so any text is one
key, and an id of another table is refused.

items.name: link
items.docs: A link to a row of this table. It is not fetched.

items.name: rows
items.docs:
The rows of the table, inside a clause: `(SELECT VALUE id FROM t)`.
Each row is a record id, so a field read is a traversal. With it a
clause writes a correlated subquery or a semi join:
`visits.rows().keep_if(|v| v.patient.get().id == p.id).len()`.
An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: auth
items.docs:
The record user of the session, a row of this table, inside a
clause: `$auth.id`. `|m| m.owner.id() == users.auth()` is
`owner = $auth.id`. A session of a system user has no record
user, and `$auth.id` is `NONE`. An intrinsic: SurrealDB computes it.

items.name: text_index
items.docs:
A full-text index of the `Str` field at the path, over the
analyzer: `notes.text_index(|n| n.body, clinical)`. Give it to
`Def.text_index` and to `Query.search`.

items.name: vector_index
items.signature: Table(row), Code(row -> List(n)), { dimension : U64, distance : Distance } -> VectorIndex(row)
items.docs:
An HNSW index of the vector field at the path, of `dimension`
numbers, by `distance`: `notes.vector_index(|n| n.embedding, {
dimension: 3, distance: Cosine })`. A `List(F64)` is indexed as
`TYPE F64`, a `List(F32)` as `TYPE F32`. Give it to
`Def.vector_index` and to `Query.nearest`.

items.name: define
items.docs:
The schema builder of this table. The definition holds the type of
the row: `Code.ty_of` describes `row` at each use that fixes it, so
`customers.define()` has the description of `Customer`. A view
takes its query with `define_as`.

items.name: define_read
items.docs:
A read row of the table: the same row as the stored one, with a
`Linked` for a `Link` and with `Out` and `In` fields for the edge
tables at the row. It writes no statement. `schema` checks that it
agrees with the stored row of the table of the same name, and
reports a `BadSchema` when not:

pets : Surreal.Table(Pet)               # owner : Surreal.Linked(Owner)
stored_pets : Surreal.Table(StoredPet)  # owner : Surreal.Link(Owner)
Surreal.schema([.., stored_pets.define().done(), pets.define_read()])

items.name: define_as
items.signature: Table(out), Grouped({}, row, k), Code((k, List(row) -> out)) -> Def(out)
items.docs:
The definition of a view: `DEFINE TABLE name TYPE NORMAL AS SELECT
.. GROUP BY ..`. Each write to the source table updates it. It
takes no rule, and its query reads a whole table, not a range
(SurrealDB refuses a range in a view). The row type is the result
of `per_group`:

daily = Surreal.view("vital_daily")
daily_def = daily.define_as(Surreal.from(vitals).group_by(day_of), day_line).done()

items.name: code_primitives
items.docs: The cut of `update` and `delete` clauses (see `Surreal.code_primitives`).

items.name: insert
items.signature: Table(row), List(row) -> Try(Prepared(List(row)), Error) where [row.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (row, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), row.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
One transaction that inserts every row, with the values the
compiler's derived encoder writes. An absent optional field is a key
left out. The `id` field stays in the row: it is the record key.
The result is the rows as stored, with the fields that the
database computes: `BEGIN`, the `INSERT`, `COMMIT`, and a
failure is the insert's.

items.name: insert_new
items.signature: Table({ id : Str, ..new }), List(new) -> Try(Prepared(List(Created({ id : Str, ..new }, new))), Error) where [new.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (new, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), new.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
[Table.insert] of rows whose keys the server makes, as
[Table.create_new] does: each row without its `id`. The result is
the rows as stored, in the order of `rows`.

items.name: create
items.signature: Table(row), row -> Try(Prepared(List(row)), Error) where [row.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (row, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), row.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
A new row at `table:⟨id⟩`, or for an edge table the edge between
the rows of `from` and `to`: `CREATE`, `RELATE`. It fails when
the row exists. The result is the row as stored.

items.name: create_new
items.signature: Table({ id : Str, ..new }), new -> Try(Prepared(List(Created({ id : Str, ..new }, new))), Error) where [new.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (new, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), new.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
A new row whose key the server makes: the row without its `id`.
`CREATE t CONTENT ..`, or for an edge table `RELATE` with no key.
The key is the default of `id` in the schema
(`.default_by(|r| r.id, |_| Surreal.Rand.ulid())`), or else
SurrealDB's random 20 characters. The result is the row as
stored: its `Id`, and its other fields.

items.name: upsert
items.signature: Table(row), row -> Try(Prepared(List(row)), Error) where [row.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (row, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), row.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
The row at `table:⟨id⟩`, replaced when it exists and made when
not. The result is the row as stored after the write.

items.name: replace
items.signature: Table(row), row -> Try(Prepared(List(row)), Error) where [row.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (row, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), row.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
The row at `table:⟨id⟩`, replaced by this one when it exists:
`UPDATE .. CONTENT`. The result is the row as stored after the
write, or none when the key has no row.

items.name: insert_or_update
items.signature: Table(row), List(row), Code((row, row -> row)) -> Try(Prepared(List(row)), Error) where [row.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (row, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), row.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
Insert rows, and where a row with the same key exists, change the
stored row instead: `INSERT INTO t [..] ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE ..`.
The patch takes the new row and the stored one, `|new, old| {
..old, visits: old.visits + new.visits }`, and is translated as
the patch of `update` is: each changed field is an item, and the
new row is `$input`. One transaction, as `insert` is. The result
is the rows as stored. SurrealDB 3.3.4 takes a duplicate to be the
same record key; a row that only repeats the value of a unique
index is refused (`Unique`). It evaluates the clause once with no
stored row before it reads one, and then `old.visits + 1` is an
error, so each item is guarded with `IF id != NONE` (verified). A
relation table is refused.

items.name: patch_at
items.signature: Table(row), Id(row), List(Patch(row)) -> Try(Prepared(List(row)), Error) where [row.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
Replay patches on the row with this key, in order: `UPDATE
t:⟨k⟩ PATCH [..]`, a JSON Patch. The patches are those of
`Query.live_diff` (`Patch`), so a client can apply the changes
that another client saw. A patch of a create (the replace of `""`
by the whole row) sets each field. These are refused when the
statement is built: a patch of another row, a patch of a delete
(`delete_at` is that), an op below `/id`, and a `change` op, a
text diff that the ORM reads and does not write. A path that the
row does not have, or a value of another type, is the server's
error. The result is the row as stored, or none for a key with
no row.

items.name: patch_ops_at
items.signature: Table(row), Id(row), List(Op) -> Try(Prepared(List(row)), Error) where [row.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
[Table.patch_at] of ops that the app made, `Replace(["tag"],
Cbor.Value.Text("x"))`.

items.name: merge_at
items.signature: Table(row), Id(row), partial -> Try(Prepared(List(row)), Error) where [partial.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (partial, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), row.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
Merge a record into the row with this key: `UPDATE t:⟨k⟩ MERGE
{ .. }`. The record is a value of the app with only the fields
to change, and an object field in it is merged into the stored
object, key by key. `set_at` writes the same, but each field as
a clause; this takes the record whole. Roc has no type for a
record of some of the row's fields, so a field the row does not
have, or of another type, is the server's error (`SCHEMAFULL`
checks a `MERGE`), and `id` is refused. A union field is merged
key by key too, so the keys of its old arm stay (verified): change
a union with `set_at`, as `update` does. The result is the row as
stored, or none for a key with no row.

items.name: upsert_merge_at
items.signature: Table(row), Id(row), partial -> Try(Prepared(List(row)), Error) where [partial.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (partial, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), row.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
[Table.merge_at] where the row is made when the key has none:
`UPSERT t:⟨k⟩ MERGE { .. }`, so the record must hold every field
that the schema requires.

items.name: merge
items.signature: Table(row), Code(row -> Bool), partial -> Try(Prepared(List(row)), Error) where [partial.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (partial, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), row.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
[Table.merge_at] in every row that the condition keeps:
`UPDATE t MERGE { .. } WHERE ..`.

items.name: edit
items.signature: Table(row), Edit(row) -> Try(Prepared(List(row)), Error) where [row.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (row, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), row.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
One write of whole rows, as the Mirror describes it (`Edit`):
`CREATE` or, for an edge, `RELATE`; `UPDATE .. CONTENT` with the
whole new row; `DELETE` of the record. The result is the row as
stored: after a create and a replace, before a delete, and none
for a replace or a delete of a row that is not there. A write
that has only the new row or the key is `replace` or `delete_at`.

items.name: ref
items.signature: Table(row), row -> Try(Ref, Error) where [row.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (row, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, []))]
items.docs: The record id of a row, as a live query reports it.

items.name: group_ref
items.signature: Table(row), k -> Try(Ref, Error) where [k.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (k, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, []))]
items.docs:
The record id of a row of a view: the values of its group key, in
the order of `GROUP BY`, which is the name order of a key record.

items.name: update
items.signature: Table(row), Code(row -> Bool), Code(row -> row) -> Write(p, row)
items.docs:
Set the fields the patch changes in every row the condition keeps.
The patch is the row with some fields replaced, `|o| { ..o, f: .. }`,
and each changed field is a `SET` item. An optional field that the
patch's row leaves out is `NONE`. `SET`, never `MERGE`, because
`MERGE` breaks a union field.

items.name: update_by
items.signature: Table(row), Code((p, row -> Bool)), Code((p, row -> row)) -> Write(p, row)
items.docs:
[Table.update] where the condition and the patch read the parameter
record, `|p, o| ..`.

items.name: set
items.signature: Table(row), Code(row -> Bool), Code(row -> patch) -> Write(p, row)
items.docs:
Set the fields of a patch in every row the condition keeps. The
patch is a record of only the fields it sets, `|o| { name: "Jo",
visits: o.visits + 1 }`, each one a `SET` item. Roc cannot type a
record of some of the row's fields, so the statement checks each
field against the row when it is built: a name the row does not
have, or another type, is `BadSchema`. An optional field takes its
value or a `Try` of it, whose `Err` makes it `NONE`.

items.name: set_by
items.signature: Table(row), Code((p, row -> Bool)), Code((p, row -> patch)) -> Write(p, row)
items.docs:
[Table.set] where the condition and the patch read the parameter
record, `|p, o| ..`.

items.name: update_at
items.signature: Table(row), Id(row), Code(row -> row) -> Write(p, row)
items.docs:
[Table.update] of the row with this key: `UPDATE vet:⟨tia⟩ SET ..`.
SurrealDB writes the one record, where a condition on the key
reads every row of the table (verified with `EXPLAIN`). A key
with no row changes nothing.

items.name: update_at_by
items.signature: Table(row), Id(row), Code((p, row -> row)) -> Write(p, row)
items.docs: [Table.update_at] where the patch reads the parameter record.

items.name: set_at
items.signature: Table(row), Id(row), Code(row -> patch) -> Write(p, row)
items.docs: [Table.set] of the row with this key: `UPDATE vet:⟨tia⟩ SET ..`.

items.name: set_at_by
items.signature: Table(row), Id(row), Code((p, row -> patch)) -> Write(p, row)
items.docs: [Table.set_at] where the patch reads the parameter record.

items.name: delete_at
items.docs:
Delete the row with this key: `DELETE vet:⟨tia⟩`. A key with no
row deletes nothing.

items.name: delete
items.docs: Delete every row the condition keeps.

items.name: delete_by
items.signature: Table(row), Code((p, row -> Bool)) -> Write(p, row)
items.docs: [Table.delete] where the condition reads the parameter record.

items.name: table
items.docs:
A table. The annotation on the binding fixes `row`:

customers : Surreal.Table(Customer)
customers = Surreal.table("customer")

items.name: relation
items.signature: Str, Table(a), Table(b) -> Table({ from : Link(a), to : Link(b), ..r })
items.docs:
An edge table from one table to another. The row has `from : Link(a)`
and `to : Link(b)`: SurrealDB's `in` and `out`, which a row cannot name
because `in` is a keyword. The type says so, so a row whose ends do not
point at the two tables, in this order, is a type error.

items.name: view
items.docs:
A table that SurrealDB keeps from a grouped query. It is read-only.
Its query is in its definition (`Table.define_as`), so the table
itself holds only the name, and a clause can read it.

items.name: fetched
items.signature: Table({ id : Str, ..others }), { id : Str, ..others } -> Link({ id : Str, ..others })
items.docs: A link that holds its row, for seed data and for a row read back.

items.name: Def
items.signature: { source : Types.Source, rules : List(Schema.Rule), problems : List(Error) }
items.docs:
A table's schema being built. Each clause is a Roc function that is
reified and translated where it is given; a clause SurrealQL cannot
hold is kept as a problem, and `schema` reports the first one.
items.head: Def(row)

items.name: source
items.docs: The schema entry of a table definition: what `Types` reads.

items.name: code_primitives
items.docs: The cut of schema clauses (see `Surreal.code_primitives`).

items.name: check
items.docs:
A row predicate, named for its error message. It is the `ASSERT`
of the one field it reads, or an event when it reads several.

items.name: assert
items.signature: Def(row), Code(row -> v), Code(v -> Bool) -> Def(row)
items.docs: A predicate on one field. Through `.?` it sees a `Try`.

items.name: assert_each
items.signature: Def(row), Code(row -> List(v)), Code(v -> Bool) -> Def(row)
items.docs: A predicate on each element of a list field.

items.name: unique
items.docs: A unique index on a path, or on a record of paths.

items.name: default
items.signature: Def(row), Code(row -> v), v -> Def(row) where [v.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (v, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, []))]
items.docs: The value a field takes when a write leaves it out: `.default(|c| c.tags, [])`.

items.name: default_by
items.signature: Def(row), Code(row -> v), Code(row -> v) -> Def(row)
items.docs:
As `default`, with the value an expression of the row, which may call
`Rand`: `.default_by(|o| o.key, |_| Surreal.Rand.ulid())`.

items.name: computed
items.signature: Def(row), Code(row -> v), Code(row -> v) -> Def(row)
items.docs: A field SurrealDB computes on every write from the row.

items.name: created_now
items.docs: The time of the row's first write, which later writes keep.

items.name: on_delete
items.signature: Def(row), Table(t), [Reject, Unset, Cascade, Ignore] -> Def(row)
items.docs:
What deleting a row of `target` does to every link from this table
to it, at any depth. Without one, the delete is rejected.

items.name: on_delete_at
items.signature: Def(row), Code(row -> l), [Reject, Unset, Cascade, Ignore] -> Def(row)
items.docs: The same for the one link at a path; it wins over `on_delete`.

items.name: changefeed
items.docs:
A change history of this length: `CHANGEFEED <n>ns` on the table line.
SurrealDB keeps it, and `SHOW CHANGES FOR TABLE` reads it.

items.name: text_index
items.docs:
The full-text index of `Table.text_index`: `DEFINE INDEX .. FIELDS
body FULLTEXT ANALYZER clinical BM25 HIGHLIGHTS`. `schema`
refuses an analyzer that it is not given.

items.name: vector_index
items.docs:
The vector index of `Table.vector_index`: `DEFINE INDEX .. FIELDS
embedding HNSW DIMENSION 3 DIST COSINE TYPE F64`. SurrealDB then
refuses a write of a vector of another dimension (verified).

items.name: permit
items.docs:
A permission of the table for a record user: the rows that the
condition keeps, for each of `actions`, which may read the
session (`Table.auth`, `Auth`). `.permit([Select], |m|
m.owner.id() == users.auth())` is `PERMISSIONS FOR select WHERE
owner = $auth.id`. A table with no permission keeps SurrealDB's
default, and a table with one names each action: an action that
no permission names is `NONE`. A system user is not checked.

items.name: permit_full
items.docs: [Def.permit] of every row: `FOR .. FULL`.

items.name: permit_field
items.signature: Def(row), Code(row -> v), List(Action), Code(row -> Bool) -> Def(row)
items.docs:
A permission of one field (`select`, `create`, `update`): the rows
whose field a record user reads or writes. A field with no
permission is `FULL`, SurrealDB's default for a field. A field
that a select may not read is not in its row: give it a type
that reads with it left out (`?:`), or select the other fields.

items.name: deny_field
items.docs:
[Def.permit_field] of no row: `FOR .. NONE`, such as the hash of a
password that no record user reads.

items.name: done
items.docs: The definition, ready for `schema`.

items.name: Defined
items.docs: A finished table definition.
items.head: Defined

items.name: Action
items.docs:
What a permission is for (`Def.permit`): `Select`, `Create`,
`Update` or `Delete`.
items.head: Action

items.name: Access
items.docs:
A record access method of the database, by its name: `DEFINE ACCESS
name ON DATABASE TYPE RECORD`. A record user signs up with the
variables `up` and signs in with `on`, both records: the
annotation on the binding fixes them, as for a table.

accounts : Surreal.Access({ email : Str, pass : Str }, { email : Str, pass : Str })
accounts = Surreal.access("account")
items.head: Access(up, on)

items.name: code_primitives
items.docs: The cut of the signup and the signin (see `Surreal.code_primitives`).

items.name: define
items.signature: Access(up, on), Table({ id : Str, ..new }), Code((up -> new)), Code((on, { id : Str, ..new } -> Bool)) -> AccessDef
items.docs:
The definition of the access method, over the rows of a table of
users. The signup is the new row, without its `id`, from the
variables, each a `$name`: `|v| { email: v.email, pass:
Surreal.Hash.argon2(v.pass) }` is `CREATE user CONTENT { email:
$email, pass: crypto::argon2::generate($pass) }`, and it may
call `Rand` and `Hash.argon2`, as a write. The signin keeps the
row of the user, as `filter_by` does: `|v, u| u.email == v.email
and Surreal.Hash.argon2_matches(u.pass, v.pass)` is `SELECT *
FROM user WHERE email = $email AND crypto::argon2::compare(pass,
$pass)`. The server runs both as a system user, so the
permissions of the table do not apply to them.

items.name: sign_up
items.signature: Access(up, on), { ns : Str, db : Str }, up -> Login where [up.Cbor.Writable]
items.docs:
The login of a new record user (`Session.open!`): `signup` with
the variables of the record.

items.name: sign_in
items.signature: Access(up, on), { ns : Str, db : Str }, on -> Login where [on.Cbor.Writable]
items.docs: The login of a record user: `signin` with the variables of the record.

items.name: access
items.docs:
An access method of this name. The annotation on the binding fixes
its variables.

items.name: AccessDef
items.signature: { name : Str, table : Str, content : Try(Str, Error), cond : Try(Str, Error), token : Try(U64, [Unset]), session : Try(U64, [Unset]) }
items.docs: The definition of an access method being built (`Access.define`).
items.head: AccessDef

items.name: token_for
items.docs:
How long a token of a signup or a signin is valid:
`DURATION FOR TOKEN`. SurrealDB's default is 1 hour.

items.name: session_for
items.docs:
How long a session that signed in is valid: `DURATION FOR
SESSION`. SurrealDB's default is no end.

items.name: done
items.docs: The definition, ready for `schema`.

items.name: schema
items.docs:
The schema script of every function and table: functions, tables,
fields, indexes, events, in that order. The list is also where a link
finds its target table.

items.name: Clause
items.docs:
A clause is written when its statement is, because the spelling of a
parameter is chosen then: `$name` for a driver, the literal for a script.
items.head: Clause

items.name: Rows
items.signature: { now : Try(Translate.Binding, Error), before : Try(Translate.Binding, Error), reach : Translate.Reach }
items.docs:
The row of a query at the two records a statement reads it at:
`now` is the row the statement reads, and `before` is that row
before the write that a live query reports, `$before`. `reach` is
the row as a live query reads it, for the tables that the clauses
read (`Translate.reads`).
items.head: Rows

items.name: Filter
items.docs:
A filter is written when its statement is, over one of the `Rows`.
The result is a binding, so a live query can put an infix filter in
parentheses.
items.head: Filter

items.name: Query
items.docs:
A query over the rows of a table, taking parameters of type `p`.
`source` says what a clause reads its row as, now and before a write
(see `Rows`): the table row, the pair of a row and its edges once
`outgoing` or `incoming` ran, or a result row of `Selected.query`. It is an error when that result row has no
SurrealQL form. `watched` are the other tables that a live query
watches (see `Watched`).
items.head: Query(p, row)

items.name: code_primitives
items.docs: The cut of filters, projections and keys (see `Surreal.code_primitives`).

items.name: filter
items.signature: Query(p, row), Code(row -> Bool) -> Query(p, row)
items.docs: Keep the rows the function is true for: `WHERE`.

items.name: filter_by
items.signature: Query(p, row), Code((p, row -> Bool)) -> Query(p, row)
items.docs:
A filter that reads the parameter record, its first argument. Each
field it reads is a `$name` that `prepare` gives a `LET`.

items.name: outgoing
items.signature: Query(p, a), Table({ from : Link(a), ..e }) -> Query(p, (a, List({ from : Link(a), ..e })))
items.docs:
The row and its edges in `edges`, `->edges`. The row becomes the pair
`(row, List(edge))`, which a clause takes apart with a tuple pattern.
The edge row's `from` links to `a`, so edges that leave another
table are a type error.

items.name: incoming
items.signature: Query(p, b), Table({ to : Link(b), ..e }) -> Query(p, (b, List({ to : Link(b), ..e })))
items.docs:
As `outgoing`, with the edges that point at the row: `<-edges`. The
edge row's `to` links to `b`.

items.name: and_outgoing
items.signature: Query(p, (a, List(x))), Table({ from : Link(a), ..e }) -> Query(p, (a, List(x), List({ from : Link(a), ..e })))
items.docs:
A second edge table on the row: after `outgoing` or `incoming`,
the edges that leave the row in `edges` too. The row becomes the
triple `(row, List(e1), List(edge))`. A live query watches both
edge tables. For more edge tables, take a read row with an `Out`
or `In` field for each.

items.name: and_incoming
items.signature: Query(p, (b, List(x))), Table({ to : Link(b), ..e }) -> Query(p, (b, List(x), List({ to : Link(b), ..e })))
items.docs: As `and_outgoing`, with the edges that point at the row.

items.name: search
items.signature: Query(p, row), FullText(row), Str -> Query(p, (row, Hit))
items.docs:
The rows whose text matches the terms, by the full-text index:
`WHERE body @1@ 'limping'`. The row becomes the pair `(row,
hit)`, and the hit reads what the search knows of the row,
`search::score(1)` and the highlights: `select(|(n, hit)| { id:
n.id, score: hit.score() })`. The library numbers the search,
so no clause writes the number. The index, the search and the
hit are of one row type, so a query has one search, and no
`nearest`. The Roc meaning of which rows it keeps is
`Analyzer.matches`. A live query refuses it.

items.name: nearest
items.signature: Query(p, row), VectorIndex(row), List(F64), Knn -> Query(p, (row, Near))
items.docs:
The `k` rows whose vector is nearest the probe, by the vector
index: `WHERE embedding <|2,40|> [..]` (`Approx`), or `<|2,COSINE|>`
(`Exact`), among the rows that the other filters keep (verified).
The row becomes the pair `(row, near)`, and `near.distance()`
is `vector::distance::knn()`. A probe of another dimension than
the index's is refused. The Roc meaning of `Exact` is the rows
sorted by their `Vector` distance from the probe, the first `k`.
A live query refuses it.

items.name: between
items.signature: Query(p, { id : TimeKey(s), ..others }), s, Datetime, Datetime -> Query(p, { id : TimeKey(s), ..others }) where [s.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (s, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, []))]
items.docs:
The rows of one series of a time series with `from <= time < to`:
`FROM t:[series, from]..[series, to]`. It reads the range of keys, not
the whole table. A query takes one `between`.

items.name: select
items.signature: Query(p, row), Code(row -> out) -> Selected(p, out)
items.docs:
The columns of the result. The function returns a record, and its
fields name the columns, in name order: `SELECT e AS f, ..`. A whole
record is one column per field of its Roc type: `select(|r| r)` is
`SELECT record::id(id) AS id, name, ..`, where `id` is the key, as
the row holds it, and a field that SurrealDB has but the type does
not is not selected. The same holds for a linked row
(`|p| p.owner.get()`) and an object (`|v| v.contact`).

items.name: select_value
items.signature: Query(p, row), Code(row -> v) -> Selected(p, v)
items.docs:
One value per row: `SELECT VALUE e`. A whole row of a table, as
`|r| r` or `|e| e.to.get()`, is the object of the fields of its
Roc type, `SELECT VALUE { id: record::id(id), name, .. }`, so that
`id` is the key, as `select(|r| r)` gives it. `order_by` reads a
value that is a path of fields of the source row (see `ResultOrder`).

items.name: group_by
items.signature: Query(p, row), Code(row -> k) -> Grouped(p, row, k)
items.docs:
Group the rows by what the function returns: a value, or a record of
them.

items.name: totals
items.signature: Query(p, row), Code(List(row) -> out) -> Totals(p, out)
items.docs:
The totals of the rows, as one result: `GROUP ALL`. The function
takes the rows as a `List(row)`, as the one of `aggregate` does:
`rows.len()` is `count()`, and `rows.map(f).sum()` is
`math::sum(f)`. The result is one row also for no rows, with the
values that SurrealDB gives (verified on 3.3.4): a count and a
sum are 0, and a mean, a standard deviation and a variance are
`NaN`. That is why `group_by(|_| {})` is refused: a group of no
rows is no group. `math::median` of no rows is `NONE`, so it is
refused.

items.name: live_diff
items.signature: Query(p, row), p -> Try(DiffWatch(row), Error) where [p.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (p, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, []))]
items.docs:
Escape hatch: the patches of each write to the stored rows that the
filters keep, `LIVE SELECT DIFF`. It takes no projection, so it is
on `Query`. A row that no longer matches sends nothing, and a row
that starts to match sends only the ops of the write. It watches
the table only, not the tables that the filters read.

items.name: Grouped
items.signature: { query : Query(p, row), key : Code(row -> k) }
items.docs: Rows grouped by a key, waiting for what to compute per group.
items.head: Grouped(p, row, k)

items.name: code_primitives
items.docs:
The cut of the per-group function, which reads the group's rows
(see `Surreal.code_primitives`).

items.name: aggregate
items.signature: Grouped(p, row, k), Code((k, List(row) -> out)) -> Selected(p, out)
items.docs:
One result row per group. The function takes the key and the group's
rows as a `List(row)`: `rows.len()` is `count()`, and
`rows.map(f).sum()` is `math::sum(f)`.

items.name: Totals
items.docs:
The one row of `Query.totals`. It has no `filter`, `order_by`,
`limit` or `live`: a row that is always there is not a list.
items.head: Totals(p, out)

items.name: to_surql
items.docs: The statement, `GROUP ALL`.

items.name: prepare
items.signature: Totals(p, out), p -> Try(Prepared(out), Error) where [p.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (p, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), out.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
As `Selected.prepare`, and the result is the row itself: the
database always gives one.

items.name: ResultOrder
items.docs:
What `order_by` reads a result row as, given the key: the binding of
the row, or why SurrealDB cannot order by the key. `ORDER BY` takes a
field path only, and it reads it as SurrealDB reads it (verified on
3.3.4): a top-level name is a column of the result, and a longer path
is read off the source row. A call is a parse error, and a path into
an aliased column, or through a record link (`owner.name`), is
accepted and does not order: the rows come in the same order for
`ASC` and `DESC`.
items.head: ResultOrder

items.name: Selected
items.signature:
{
		target : Target,
		filters : List(Filter),
		watched : List(Watched),
		fetches : List(Str),
		groups : List(Clause),
		columns : Clause,
		value : Clause,
		intrinsic : List(Str),
		results : ResultOrder,
		rows : ResultRow,
		order : List(Clause),
		limit : [Unlimited, Limit(U64)],
		start : [FromFirst, Start(U64)],
	}
items.docs:
A query with its result columns fixed. `fetches` are the paths of
`Unchecked.fetch`. `value` is a result row as one SurrealQL value, the
`row` of a live query, or why it has none. `results` is what
`order_by` reads a result row as, and `rows` is what `filter` and
`query` read it as.
items.head: Selected(p, out)

items.name: code_primitives
items.docs: The cut of a filter of the result rows (see `Surreal.code_primitives`).

items.name: order_by
items.signature: Selected(p, out), Code(out -> k), [Asc, Desc] -> Selected(p, out)
items.docs:
Order by one column of a result row: `|r| r.rate`. Several calls
order by the first, then the second. SurrealDB's `ORDER BY` takes a
field path, so any other key is refused when the statement is
built (see `ResultOrder`).

items.name: filter
items.signature: Selected(p, out), Code(out -> Bool) -> Selected(p, out)
items.docs:
Keep the result rows the function is true for. Before a group, a
limit or a start, a result row is one source row projected, so
this is a filter of the source row in the same `WHERE`: the
predicate reads the projection's fields. After one, it is the
`WHERE` of an outer query over a subquery (`Selected.query`). After
a group, that is SQL's `HAVING`.

items.name: query
items.docs:
The result rows as the rows of a new query, which every `Query`
method reads as the type `out`:

| The result | The new query |
| --- | --- |
| A projection with no order, limit, start or fetch | The same `SELECT`. A clause reads the projection's fields over the source row |
| Any other | A subquery, `FROM (SELECT ..)`: the target `Sub` |

The target keeps the two apart, because a `LIVE SELECT` takes no
subquery.

items.name: limit
items.docs:
At most this many rows: `LIMIT n`. The rows after it are a
`Limited`, which has no `order_by`, `limit` or `start` (see
`Started`).

items.name: start
items.docs:
Skip this many rows first: `START n`. The rows after it are a
`Started`, which takes a `limit` and no `order_by` or `start`.

items.name: to_surql
items.docs: The statement with a `$name` for each parameter it reads.

items.name: prepare
items.signature: Selected(p, out), p -> Try(Prepared(List(out)), Error) where [p.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (p, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), out.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
The statement with a `LET` for each field of the parameter
record, and the type of its result: the result rows, each read
as `out`. The record is the type the filters read, so a
parameter a filter reads is a field the record has.
`Session.run!` runs it, and `Prepared.statement` is its text.

items.name: prepare_one
items.signature: Selected(p, out), p -> Try(Prepared(Try(out, [NotFound])), Error) where [p.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (p, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), out.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
`prepare` of a query of one key (`Table.at`): the row, or
`NotFound` when the table has no row with the key. Any other
query can return several rows, so it is refused.

items.name: live
items.signature: Selected(p, out), p, List(Defined) -> Try(Watch(out), Error) where [p.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (p, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, []))]
items.docs:
The rows of the query, kept current: the twin of `prepare`. A `LIVE SELECT` on the table, and one on each other table that the rows read (see `Watched`), report every write that changes the result. Each notice holds the row and the filter `now`. The filter is also read on `$before`, so a row that no longer matches is reported: `LIVE SELECT VALUE { row: , now:

} FROM t WHERE

OR ($before IS NOT NONE AND

)` The guard is necessary: a filter that reads `$before` of a `CREATE` fails, and SurrealDB then sends nothing (verified). `tables` are the definitions that `Surreal.schema` takes: a link of the row finds its table there, as in the schema.

items.name: live_raw
items.signature: Selected(p, out), p -> Try(RawWatch(out), Error) where [p.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (p, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, []))]
items.docs:
Escape hatch: the server's own events for the rows of the query.
There is no snapshot and no `$before`, so a row that no longer
matches sends nothing, a row that starts to match is `Updated`,
and a write to an edge table, or to a table that the rows read,
sends nothing.

items.name: Started
items.docs:
The rows of a `Selected` after `start`. SurrealQL writes its clauses
in one order, `ORDER BY`, `LIMIT`, `START`, and runs them in the order
`ORDER BY`, `START`, `LIMIT`. A chain of Roc steps reads as the steps
in turn, as `List.drop_first` then `List.take_first`, so the types
take only the chains that SurrealQL runs as they read: `order_by` any
number of times, then `start` at most once, then `limit` at most once.
`.limit(2).order_by(..)` (which SurrealDB runs as order, then limit),
`.limit(10).start(20)` and a second `limit` are type errors. `filter`
and `query` read the rows as a subquery, so a chain goes on from
there: `.limit(3).filter(..)`, `.limit(3).query().select(|r| r).order_by(..)`.
A live query takes no limit or start, so neither type has `live`.
items.head: Started(p, out)

items.name: limit
items.docs: At most this many of the rows: `START s LIMIT n`.

items.name: filter
items.signature: Started(p, out), Code(out -> Bool) -> Selected(p, out)
items.docs: As `Selected.filter`: the `WHERE` of a query over the rows.

items.name: query
items.docs: As `Selected.query`: the rows as a subquery.

items.name: prepare
items.signature: Started(p, out), p -> Try(Prepared(List(out)), Error) where [p.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (p, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), out.Cbor.Readable(errs)]

items.name: Limited
items.docs:
The rows of a `Selected` after `limit`: no more `order_by`, `limit`
or `start` (see `Started`).
items.head: Limited(p, out)

items.name: filter
items.signature: Limited(p, out), Code(out -> Bool) -> Selected(p, out)
items.docs: As `Selected.filter`: the `WHERE` of a query over the rows.

items.name: query
items.docs: As `Selected.query`: the rows as a subquery.

items.name: prepare
items.signature: Limited(p, out), p -> Try(Prepared(List(out)), Error) where [p.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (p, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), out.Cbor.Readable(errs)]

items.name: Write
items.signature: { build : (Str -> Str) -> Try(Str, Error), gives : [After, Before], edge : Bool }
items.docs:
A write that reads a clause: an update or a delete. `gives` is the
row that `prepare` returns: the row after an update, the row before
a delete. `edge` is true for a relation table.
items.head: Write(p, row)

items.name: to_surql
items.docs: The statement with a `$name` for each parameter it reads.

items.name: prepare
items.signature: Write(p, row), p -> Try(Prepared(List(row)), Error) where [p.encoder_for : Encode.Format -> (p, Encode.State -> Try(Encode.State, [])), row.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
The statement with a `LET` for each field of the parameter
record, and the type of its result: the rows that the write
changed, as stored. An update returns each row after the write, and a delete
each row before it: `RETURN AFTER`, `RETURN BEFORE`.

items.name: Statement
items.signature: { surql : Str, lets : List({ name : Str, value : Ql.Value }), inlined : Str, intrinsic : List(Str) }
items.docs:
A statement ready for a driver: the text with a `$name` per parameter,
the value each name is bound to, and the same text with the values
written in. `surql` has no final `;`. `intrinsic` names the columns of
its result that read an intrinsic (`intrinsic_columns`): SurrealDB
computes them, and Roc has no value for them.
items.head: Statement

items.name: to_script
items.docs: What a script holds: a `LET` line per parameter, then the statement.

items.name: block
items.docs:
One block of a script that `check.py` runs: the header line, the
directive lines (`-- ordered`, `-- roc: ..`), then the script. A
statement whose result has columns that read an intrinsic says so
in `-- intrinsic: a, b`: a `-- roc:` literal may leave those out,
and only those.

items.name: Prepared
items.signature: { statement : Statement, count : U64, atomic : [No, Whole, Parts(List(U64))], read : List(Outcome) -> Try(out, Error) }
items.docs:
A statement with the type of its result: what every query and
write gives, and what a session runs (`Session.run!`). `statement` and `count` are the
statements after the `LET`s, without a `BEGIN` and a `COMMIT`, and
`read` reads their results, in order, as `out`. `atomic` says how
they run: on their own (`No`), or in a transaction, whose failure is
the error of the statement that failed it (`Whole`, an insert) or
`Aborted` with its place (`Parts`, the count of the statements of
each part of `Transaction.commit`).

| Made by | `out` | The result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Selected.prepare` | `List(out)` | The result rows |
| `Write.prepare` | `List(row)` | The rows after an update, the rows before a delete |
| `Selected.prepare_one` | `Try(out, [NotFound])` | The row of the key of `Table.at`, or `NotFound` |
| `Table.create`, `Table.edit` | `List(row)` | The row after a create, a relate or a replace, the row before a delete. A replace or a delete of a row that is not there gives none |
| `Table.upsert`, `Table.insert` | `List(row)` | The rows that the write wrote |
| `Table.replace` | `List(row)` | The row after the write, or none for a key with no row |
| `Table.create_new`, `Table.insert_new` | `List(Created(row, new))` | The rows that the write made, each with the key that the server gave it |
| `Surreal.bind_captured` | `List(row)` | The rows of `select_where` |
