items.name: Binding
items.signature:
[
		Row({ at : Str, of : [Doc([Of(Str), Unnamed]), Ref(Code.Ty), Obj], edge : Bool }),
		WithEdges(Binding, List(Binding)),
		ListOf({ at : Str, items : Items }),
		Union({ at : Str, variants : List({ name : Str, payloads : List(Code.Ty) }) }),
		Maybe(Str),
		Params,
		Group(Binding),
		Column(Str),
		Moment(Str),
		Expr(Str),
		Infix(Str),
		Fields(List({ name : Str, binding : Binding })),
		Function({ name : Str, row : U32 }),
		Table({ name : Str, edge : Bool }),
	]
items.docs:
What a value in a reified function stands for.

`Row` is a record at a place: `Doc` is the record a statement is over
(`""` for the row itself, `$after`, `$this`), with the name of its
table for the row a statement reads (`table_row`), `Ref` is a record
id that a read traverses (`customer` after `Link.get`, an edge `$v1`),
with the type of the record it points at, and `Obj` is an object inside a
record. `edge` says the record is a relation, whose `from` and `to` are
SurrealDB's `in` and `out`. `Expr` is a value that needs no parentheses
around it as an operand, and `Infix` one that does. `Column` is
`rows.map(f)` over a `Group`: the expression `f` reads, that each
aggregate writes for itself. `Moment` is the text of a datetime, and
holds the datetime expression. `Function` is a database function made
with `Surreal.db_fn`: its name, and the row of its Roc body. `Table`
is a table of `Surreal.table`, `relation` or `view`: its name, and
whether it is an edge table.
items.head: Binding

items.name: Items
items.signature: [Values, Made, Records({ edge : Bool, row : [Typed(Code.Ty), Untyped] })]
items.docs:
What the elements of a list are: values at a path, values that the
clause made (`map`, a list literal), whose text is whole already, or
record ids that a read traverses. `edge` says the records are edges,
and `row` is their type when the list has one: the whole list is then
the fields of the type of each record, `list.{ id: record::id(id), .. }`.
items.head: Items

items.name: Step
items.docs:
One step of a field path: `items[*].qty` is `Field("items")`, `Each`,
`Field("qty")`.
items.head: Step

items.name: Call
items.signature: { owner : Str, method : Str, id : Code.PrimId, evidence : List(Code.Evidence) }
items.docs: A `Prim` of a description: the call of a primitive.
items.head: Call

items.name: Form
items.signature:
[
		Builtin({ owner : Str, method : Str }),
		Function({ surql : Str, random : Bool }),
		Aggregate(Str),
		Operator(Str),
		Percentile,
		Uuid,
		TimeGroup,
		LinkGet,
		LinkId,
		IdEq,
		IdKey,
		IdTable,
		DatetimeOrder,
		SeriesOf,
		TimeOf,
		CallDbFn,
		TableOf,
		RelationOf,
		Rows,
		RecordOf,
		Variable(Str),
		Render({ args : List(Str), evidence : List(Code.Evidence) } -> Try(Str, Str)),
	]
items.docs:
What the call of a primitive is in SurrealQL. The translator looks a
call up by its `id` (`Code.prim` of the definition), and never by its
owner and method, which name it in a refusal only: a module's own
`Bool` with a `not` has another id, so its `not` is not `!`.

`Builtin` is a builtin of Roc (`Translate.builtins`), under the name
the translator's rules for builtins use. The ids of `Surreal`'s cut
come from `Surreal.library`, as this module cannot import `Surreal`:
`Function` is one SurrealQL function of the same arguments, which gives
a new value on every call when `random` is set, `Aggregate` one over a
list or a group's column, and `Operator` an operator between two
operands. `Variable` is a value of the session that the statement
reads, such as `$auth.id`, whatever the arguments: a table that
types it. The rest are each one function of the cut. `Render` is an
extension's (`Translate.extension`): it takes the SurrealQL of each
argument and the evidence of the call, and gives the SurrealQL of the
call, or why it has none.
items.head: Form

items.name: Extension
items.signature: { prims : List({ prim : Code.PrimId, form : Form }) }
items.docs:
Forms by the ids of the primitives they are for. `Surreal.library` is
the one of `Surreal`'s cut, and an app or a glue package makes one
for the functions of its own types with `Translate.extension`.
items.head: Extension

items.name: extension
items.signature: { prims : List({ prim : Code.PrimId, render : { args : List(Str), evidence : List(Code.Evidence) } -> Try(Str, Str) }) } -> Extension
items.docs: An extension of the functions it renders, each by its id.

items.name: forms
items.signature: List({ prim : Code.PrimId, form : Form }) -> Extension
items.docs: An extension of any forms: the one `Surreal.library` makes.

items.name: form
items.docs:
The form of the primitive `id`: a builtin's, or the one the first
extension that names `id` gives it.

items.name: is_equality
items.docs: Whether the primitive `id` is `==` of a builtin or of an `Id`.

items.name: builtins
items.docs:
The builtins a clause may call, by the ids of their definitions, with
the names `Translate.builtin` reads them by. A method a type of these
does not have is not listed.

items.name: named
items.signature: Str, List((Str, Code.PrimId)) -> List((Code.PrimId, { owner : Str, method : Str }))

items.name: Env
items.signature:
{
		graph : Code.Graph,
		params : List(Binding),
		row : U32,
		nodes : List({ id : U32, binding : Binding, ty : Try(Code.Ty, [Untyped]) }),
		param : Str -> Str,
		depth : U64,
		random : Bool,
		view : [Plain, View, Totals],
		self : [Inside({ row : U32, name : Str }), Outside],
		extensions : List(Extension),
	}
items.docs:
What the translation of one row's tree reads: the graph its calls name,
what the row's parameters and kept nodes stand for, and how a parameter
of the statement is spelled. `self` is the database function whose body
this is, so a call of its own row is `fn::name(..)`. `view` is `View` for
the columns of a view, which take fewer aggregates. `extensions` give
the forms of the calls that are not builtins (`Translate.form`).
items.head: Env

items.name: document
items.docs:
The record a statement runs over: the table row (`""`), `$after` in an
event, `$this` in a field definition. `edge` is set for a relation table.

items.name: table_row
items.docs:
The row of the table `name` that a statement reads. A comparison of
its key with a value given to the statement compares the record id
(`Translate.key_compare`).

items.name: outgoing
items.docs:
The edges of a relation table from the record at `at`: `->t` going
out, `<-t` coming in, `$before<-t` from the row before a write. Each
element is an edge record.

items.name: at
items.docs:
A value at a SurrealQL expression, bound by its type: a record is a
place to read fields from, a list takes list operations, a union is
matched, a `Try` (an optional field) is tested, anything else is a
scalar. `at("$value", ty)` is the value of a field `ASSERT`.

items.name: items_of
items.docs:
The elements of a list of type `list_ty` read off a record: the
records of a read view (`List(Linked(r))`), or values.

items.name: records
items.docs:
The elements of a list of record ids of type `list_ty`: the rows of a
table, or the edges of a read view's `Out` and `In` fields.

items.name: variable
items.docs: A statement parameter `p.name` as a `LET` variable: `$name`.

items.name: input_name
items.docs: The name of captured value `k`, numbered from 1: `_1`, `_2`, ...

items.name: evaluate
items.signature: List(Extension), Code.Graph, List(Binding), (Str -> Str) -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A reified function applied to what its parameters stand for. A clause
that reads rows may not call `Rand`: it would give other rows each time.

items.name: row_value
items.signature: List(Extension), Code.Graph, List(Binding), (Str -> Str) -> Try(Str, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The same, as one SurrealQL expression, for a value that SurrealDB gives to
one row: a default, a computed field or an update. `Rand` is allowed.

items.name: run
items.signature: List(Extension), Code.Graph, List(Binding), (Str -> Str), Bool, [Plain, View, Totals] -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)

items.name: function_defs
items.signature: List(Extension), Code.Graph -> Try(List({ name : Str, params : List(Code.Ty), result : Code.Ty, body : Str }), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A database function and every database function its body calls, each
once: the name, the types of the parameters `$a1`, `$a2`, .. and of the
result, and the body as one SurrealQL expression. The root of the graph
is the constant that `Surreal.db_fn` made. A body may not call `Rand`,
because a function can run in a `WHERE`.

items.name: function_def
items.signature: List(Extension), Code.Graph, { name : Str, row : U32 } -> Try({ name : Str, params : List(Code.Ty), result : Code.Ty, body : Str }, Ql.Error)
items.docs: The body of one database function, with its own row's calls as `fn::name(..)`.

items.name: within
items.docs: An error in the body of a database function names the function.

items.name: function_values
items.docs:
The value of every `Surreal.db_fn` constant in a tree: the record of
its name and its Roc function.

items.name: function_ref
items.signature: Code.Tree -> Try({ name : Str, row : U32 }, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The name and the body row of a database function, from the record that
`Surreal.db_fn` builds. The name is a literal and the function captures
nothing, so both are fixed when the program compiles.

items.name: render
items.signature: List(Extension), Code.Graph, List(Binding), (Str -> Str) -> Try(Str, Ql.Error)
items.docs: The clause as one SurrealQL expression.

items.name: columns
items.signature: List(Extension), Code.Graph, List(Binding), (Str -> Str) -> Try(List({ name : Str, surql : Str }), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The fields of a record the clause builds, in name order, as SurrealQL
expressions. The names are Roc's; a caller spells them with `Ql.ident`.

items.name: view_columns
items.signature: List(Extension), Code.Graph, List(Binding), (Str -> Str) -> Try(List({ name : Str, surql : Str }), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The same, for the columns of a view. SurrealDB keeps fewer aggregates
in a view (`Translate.aggregate_arg`).

items.name: total_columns
items.signature: List(Extension), Code.Graph, List(Binding), (Str -> Str) -> Try(List({ name : Str, surql : Str }), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The same, for the columns of `Query.totals`: the one row of `GROUP ALL`,
which also exists for no rows (`Translate.aggregate_arg`).

items.name: fields_of
items.signature: Binding -> Try(List({ name : Str, surql : Str }), Ql.Error)

items.name: Reaching
items.signature: { graph : Code.Graph, params : List(List(Code.PrimId)), defs : List({ id : U32, value : Code.Tree, prims : List(Code.PrimId) }), rows : List(U32) }
items.docs:
Where `prims_of` walks: the graph, the primitives that each parameter
of the row stands for, the kept definitions read so far with the
primitives each one reaches, and the rows on the way, so a row that
calls itself is walked once.
items.head: Reaching

items.name: prims_of
items.docs:
The ids of the primitives that the value of a tree reaches: its own
`Prim` nodes, those of the kept definitions and the parameters it
reads, and those of each row it calls or makes a closure of.

items.name: reaching_defs
items.signature: List({ id : U32, value : Code.Tree }), Reaching -> Reaching
items.docs: The kept definitions of a block, each with the primitives it reaches.

items.name: row_prims
items.docs:
The primitives that row `row` reaches, with its first parameters
standing for `params` (a closure's captured values; the element it
is called with is the list's, which the caller walks).

items.name: column_prims
items.signature: Code.Graph -> List({ name : Str, prims : List(Code.PrimId) })
items.docs:
The primitives that each field of the record a clause returns
reaches, by the field's Roc name: one entry per column of a
`SELECT`. A clause that returns no record built in it, such as a
whole row, gives none.

items.name: record_prims
items.signature: Code.Tree, Reaching -> List({ name : Str, prims : List(Code.PrimId) })

items.name: assignments
items.signature: List(Extension), Code.Graph, List(Binding), (Str -> Str) -> Try(List({ name : Str, surql : Str }), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The `SET` list of an update patch `|o| { ..o, f: .. }`, whose last
parameter is the row. A field that reads the row's field of its own name
is unchanged and left out; every other field is `f = <expr>`, in name
order. A field whose type is a record and that the patch builds as one,
`address: { ..o.address, city: .. }`, is set field by field,
`address.city = ..`. An optional field that the patch's row leaves out
is `f = NONE`. The names are spelled as SurrealDB names them. Each
expression reads the row before the update, as in Roc: SurrealDB 3.3.4
reads the old row in each `SET` item (verified).

The reifier gives `..o` over an optional field as a presence switch on
it, with the row in each arm: without the field in `Err`, with its own
payload in `Ok` (the same switch that `Translate.presence_equality`
reads for `==`). Each arm gives its changes. A field that the arms
change alike is one item, and one they change differently is
`f = (IF <field> IS NONE THEN .. ELSE .. END)`.

items.name: patch_start
items.signature: List(Extension), Code.Graph, List(Binding), (Str -> Str) -> Try((PatchAt, Env), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
Where the patch of an update starts: the row itself, and the
environment its expressions read, where `Rand` is allowed.

items.name: set_items
items.signature: List(Change), Str -> Try(List({ name : Str, surql : Str }), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The `SET` items of the changes of a patch, or `none` when it changes
no field.

items.name: patch_assignments
items.signature: List(Extension), Code.Graph, List(Binding), (Str -> Str) -> Try(List({ name : Str, surql : Str }), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The `SET` list of a patch of only the fields it sets, `|o| { name: .. }`,
whose last parameter is the row. Each field is set as the same field
of a whole-row patch (`Translate.assignments`). Roc has no type for a
record of some of the row's fields, so this checks the patch against
the row: each field is a field of the row other than `id`, of the same
type. An optional field of the row takes its value, which makes it
present, or a `Try` of it, whose `Err` is NONE.

items.name: patch_changes
items.signature: Code.Tree, List(Types.Field), PatchAt, Env -> Try(List(Change), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The changes of a patch record, each field as the same field of the row
that `Translate.assignments` reads: a record field built as a record is
set field by field.

items.name: patch_field
items.docs: One field of a patch against the fields of the row.

items.name: fits
items.docs:
Whether a value of the patch's type `got` is a value of the row's type
`want`. The patch's type is inferred from the patch alone, so a tag is a
union of the tags it has, `Cash` is `[Cash]`, and a record leaves out
the optional fields it does not set.

items.name: PatchAt
items.signature: { path : List(Str), absent : List(List(Str)), kept : List({ id : U32, value : Code.Tree }), row : U32, edge : Bool }
items.docs:
Where a part of an update patch builds the row: the field `path` from
the row, the optional fields that a presence switch around it says are
absent, the kept definitions of the blocks around it, the row parameter
and whether the row is an edge.
items.head: PatchAt

items.name: Change
items.signature: { path : List(Str), name : Str, value : [Same, To(Str)] }
items.docs: One field of a patched row: unchanged, or set to an expression.
items.head: Change

items.name: changes
items.signature: Code.Tree, List(Types.Field), PatchAt, Env -> Try(List(Change), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The changes of the part of a patch that builds the record at `here.path`,
whose fields in the row are `fields`. A kept definition, such as a field
that `..o` keeps and the patch reads, is read as its value.

items.name: merge
items.docs:
The changes of the two arms of a presence switch on the field that
`test` reads. A field that an arm leaves out is unchanged there, because
the arm keeps the record around it. A field that the arms change alike
is that change, and one they change differently is an `IF` on the
presence. A field that one arm sets whole, while the other sets its
fields, has no one `SET` list.

items.name: whole_change
items.docs:
A part of a patch that does not build its record field by field: the
row's own value, unchanged, or a value that the field is set to. The
patch itself builds the row it returns.

items.name: field_change
items.signature: Types.Field, Try(Code.Tree, [NotFound]), PatchAt, Env -> Try(List(Change), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The change of field `f` of a record the patch builds, where `given` is
the value the record gives it. An optional field the record leaves out
is unchanged where a presence switch says the row has no such field,
and `NONE` elsewhere.

items.name: presence_field
items.signature: List(Code.Key), Code.Tree, List(Code.Tree), PatchAt -> Try({ name : Str, absent : Code.Tree, present : Code.Tree }, [NotOptional])
items.docs:
The optional field of the record at `here.path` that a switch tests for
presence, with its arm where the field is absent and its arm where it
is present: the scrutinee reads the field, and the arms are `Err` and
`Ok`.

items.name: optional_read
items.docs:
The name of the optional field that a tree reads off the record at
`here.path`, `Unwrap(OptField(name))`.

items.name: is_at
items.docs: Whether a tree is the row's own value at a field path, unchanged.

items.name: spell_path
items.docs: A field path of the row as SurrealDB names it, `address.city`.

items.name: kept_value
items.signature: Code.Tree, List({ id : U32, value : Code.Tree }) -> Code.Tree
items.docs: The tree that a read of a kept definition stands for.

items.name: body
items.docs:
A row's tree without the block around it, where the block holds one
value and no definitions.

items.name: path_of
items.docs:
The field path a path lambda reads: a chain of field reads, `.?` reads
and `List.map` with a closure that is itself a path.

items.name: paths_of
items.docs: The paths a key lambda reads: one path, or a record or tuple of them.

items.name: steps_in
items.signature: Code.Graph, List({ id : U32, value : Code.Tree }), Code.Tree -> Try(List(Step), Ql.Error)
items.docs: The steps of a path, where `defs` are the kept definitions in scope.

items.name: spell
items.docs: A path as a field definition names it: `items[*].qty`.

items.name: describe
items.docs: What an op is, for a refusal that names it.

items.name: captured
items.docs:
The SurrealQL value of a value captured from around the clause, by the
slot type the graph gives it. An `Id` is its record id, a `Datetime`
its datetime. A captured `Link` is refused. Capture its `id()` instead.
An optional field that a captured record does not hold (`Absent`) is
left out of its object, as a stored row leaves out a field that is
`NONE`. A value whose type holds an opaque type is the bytes its own
encoder wrote in `Encode.Bind` (`Surreal.select_where_with`), which
read back as `Encode.Format` writes a row.

items.name: named_str
items.signature: List({ name : Str, value : Ql.Value }), Str -> Try(Str, [Missing])

items.name: is_record
items.docs:
Whether a union payload of this type is spread next to `kind`: a
record, or a nominal of the app over one (`Types.unwrap`), as in the
schema and `Encode.tagged`. A type of `Surreal`, such as a geometry or
a `Link`, is `value`.

items.name: Reach
items.signature:
[
		At({ path : Str, lists : U64, edge : Bool, via : [Doc, Ref(Code.Ty), Records], ty : Code.Ty }),
		Fields(List({ name : Str, reach : Reach })),
		Pair(List(Reach)),
		Either(List(Reach)),
		Table({ name : Str, edge : Bool }),
		Nothing,
	]
items.docs:
What a value of a clause reads, for the tables that a live query
watches (`Translate.reads`). `At` is a place, by its `via`:

| `via` | The place |
| --- | --- |
| `Doc` | A value in a record that the statement reads: the row, a field of it, a field of a linked row after a hop |
| `Ref(row)` | A record that a link points at, before a field of it is read: a `Linked` of a read row, `link.get()`. A field read through it is a hop to a row of type `row` |
| `Records` | A list of records whose table the live query watches already: the edges of `outgoing`, `incoming`, an `Out` or an `In`, and `rows()` |

`path` is the place as a `read` statement tests it, from the row of
the statement (`items[*].product`, `<-cares_for.in`, `kennel.site`),
`lists` counts the lists on it, `edge` says it is an edge record, and
`ty` is its type. `Fields` is a record the clause built, `Pair` a row
with its edges, `Either` the value of a branch, which is one of its
arms, and `Table` a table that the clause names.
items.head: Reach

items.name: Read
items.signature: [Hop({ path : Str, target : Code.Ty, lists : U64, read : [Field(Str), Whole] }), Edges({ name : Str, node : Str })]
items.docs:
What a live query watches for one read of a clause: a hop through a
link, a read of the record at `path` that a link points at, whose
row is `target`, or the edges of an `Out` or `In` field of the row,
whose `node` is the end of an edge that is the row. `read` is the
field of that record that the clause reads, as SurrealDB spells it,
or `Whole` for the whole record.
items.head: Read

items.name: Walk
items.signature: { graph : Code.Graph, row : U32, params : List(Reach), nodes : List({ id : U32, reach : Reach }), depth : U64, extensions : List(Extension) }
items.docs:
The walk of `Translate.reads`: what the row's parameters and kept
nodes reach.
items.head: Walk

items.name: row_reach
items.docs:
The row of a table, as a clause reads it: the record at `""`. It has
the type of the parameter that reads it (`Translate.retyped`).

items.name: with_edges
items.docs:
A row and its edges in `table`, after `->` (`outgoing`) or `<-`
(`incoming`) the row's own place.

items.name: edges_reach
items.signature: { path : Str, lists : U64, edge : Bool, via : [Doc, Ref(Code.Ty), Records], ty : Code.Ty }, Str, Str -> Reach

items.name: rows_at
items.docs: The record ids of the rows of a table in a clause.

items.name: reads
items.docs:
What a clause reads through links, for the tables a live query
watches, and what its result is. A read is a field read through a
link (`Hop`), at the path of the link, and an `Out` or `In` field of
the row (`Edges`). The result is read whole: a whole linked row in it
is a hop too, and a `Link` in it is a record id. `params` are what the
parameters are. A form that the translator refuses reads nothing.

items.name: reach_lambda
items.signature: Code.Tree, Code.Tree, [Each, Kept, Found(Code.Ty), Mapped], Walk -> Reached
items.docs:
A list operation with a closure, as `Translate.lambda` reads it, and
`map_ok`: the closure's row with its element. The closure's result is
read whole. `gives` is the result of the operation: none, the list
(`keep_if`, `drop_if`), an element (`find_first`), or the closure's
result (`map_ok`).

items.name: closure_element
items.docs: The type of the element of a closure's row: its last parameter.

items.name: expand_reach
items.docs:
A row of the graph with its parameters bound, as `Translate.expand`
reads a call.

items.name: consumed
items.docs:
The arguments of an operation that reads them as values: each is
read whole.

items.name: each_arm
items.docs: A step over each arm of a branch.

items.name: retyped
items.docs: A value of the type of the parameter that reads it.

items.name: place_of
items.docs:
A place of a value of type `ty`: a `Linked` is a record that a link
points at.

items.name: member_reach
items.docs:
A field of a value, as `Translate.member` reads it. A field read off
a record that a link points at is a hop. Its `id` is the record id
the link holds, and is not.

items.name: edge_field
items.signature: { path : Str, lists : U64, edge : Bool, via : [Doc, Ref(Code.Ty), Records], ty : Code.Ty }, Str, Str, Str, Code.Ty -> Reached
items.docs:
An `Out` or `In` field: the edges of the record. The edge statement
of a live query watches the edges of the row only.

items.name: element_reach
items.docs:
The element of a list, as `Translate.lambda` binds it. An element of
a list of records is the record, and of a list of links or `Linked`
rows the list itself (`$parent.id IN wishlist`).

items.name: payload_reach
items.docs:
A payload, as `Translate.payload` reads it: the value of a `Try` is
at its place, and a union arm at `value`, unless it is a record.

items.name: read_whole
items.docs:
What a value read whole reads: each `Linked` in it, at any depth
(`Types.whole_reads`), also in the records of a list of them, and the
edges of each `Out` and `In` field of the row. A `Link` in it is its
record id.

items.name: linked_reads
items.docs:
The `Linked` rows of a whole value at `path`. The fields of an edge
after a path are spelled as at the row, `in` and `out`.

items.name: row_edges
items.docs:
The edges of each `Out` and `In` field of a whole row, and the
`Linked` rows of each edge.

items.name: text
items.docs: A binding as a SurrealQL expression that stands on its own.

items.name: operand
items.docs:
A binding as the operand of an operator: an infix expression is
parenthesised, so nesting never depends on SurrealQL's precedence.

items.name: eval
items.docs:
What one tree stands for. A kept node is computed once, where its block
defines it, and each read of it is what it stands for.

items.name: define
items.signature: List({ id : U32, value : Code.Tree }), Env -> Try(Env, Ql.Error)
items.docs: The environment with the kept definitions of a block computed, in order.

items.name: type_of
items.docs: The type of a value, where the tree or the graph states it.

items.name: is_record_value
items.docs:
Whether a value's type is a record payload (`Translate.is_record`). The
type, not the tree, decides, so a kept definition reads as its value.

items.name: is_link
items.docs: Whether a value's type is a stored `Link`.

items.name: geometry_parameter
items.docs:
Why a geometry other than a point has no SurrealQL form in a clause:
a tuple takes only number literals, and `<geometry>` of an object
fails in SurrealDB 3.3.4.

items.name: op
items.signature: Code.Op, List(Code.Tree), Code.Ty, Env -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
One operation, over the trees of its arguments and regions, with the
type of its result.

items.name: link_field
items.docs:
A field of a stored `Link`, `{ id, fetched }`, read in a clause: `link.id`
and `link.id()` are the same, the record id the link holds, which is the
link itself in SurrealQL. `fetched` is the row that the program holds,
and the database has no such field.

items.name: field
items.signature: Binding, Str, Code.Ty, Env -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)

items.name: member
items.signature: { at : Str, of : [Doc([Of(Str), Unnamed]), Ref(Code.Ty), Obj], edge : Bool }, Str, Code.Ty -> Binding
items.docs: A field of a record at a place, by the field's type.

items.name: row_columns
items.signature: Code.Ty, { at : Str, of : [Doc([Of(Str), Unnamed]), Ref(Code.Ty), Obj], edge : Bool } -> Try(List({ name : Str, surql : Str }), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The fields of a whole row of type `row_ty`, in name order, each read
off the record at `place`. Off the row a statement is over, that is
`record::id(id)` for `id`, `in` for the `from` of an edge, the field's
name for the others. `select(|r| r)` selects them, and a linked row
destructures them.

items.name: shaped
items.docs:
A whole value of type `ty`. A record or a list of records that holds
a `Linked` is the destructure of its fields, so that each linked row
in it is the fields of its type: `items.{ product: product.{ id:
record::id(id), title, .. }, qty }`. Any other value is its text.

items.name: refers_back
items.docs:
Whether a type is a `Linked` that the description gives as
`Recursive`: a read row that holds a `Linked` of itself, at this
place or in a list here.

items.name: holds_linked
items.docs:
Whether a type holds a `Linked`, or an `Out` or `In` field, other than
through a `Link`.

items.name: typed_fields
items.signature: Binding, Code.Ty -> Try(List({ name : Str, surql : Str }), Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The columns of a result row the clause built, of type `ty`. A field
that holds a `Linked` is shaped by its type (`Translate.shaped`).

items.name: whole_row
items.docs:
A whole linked row, with the fields of its Roc type and `id` as the
key, not the record id: `owner.{ id: record::id(id), name, address }`.
The value is NONE when the link is NONE.

items.name: spell_name
items.docs:
A field name as SurrealDB names it: an edge's `from` and `to` are `in`
and `out`, because `in` is a Roc keyword.

items.name: tag
items.docs:
A union literal in the union encoding of `Encode`: `'Cash'`,
`{ kind: 'Card', last4: .. }`, `{ kind: 'C', value: .. }`,
`{ kind: 'D', value: [.., ..] }`.

items.name: wrap
items.docs:
A nominal value written in the clause. An `Id` or a `Datetime` of
literals is its SurrealQL literal; a user nominal is its backing.

items.name: try_value
items.docs:
A `Try` built in a clause, as a value that may be NONE: `Ok(x)` is
`x`, and `Err(_)` is NONE, as for a `Try` read from an optional field.

items.name: payload
items.signature: Binding, Str, U64, Code.Ty -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A payload read, by the union payload rule of `Encode`: a record
payload is the union object itself, one other payload is `value`,
several are the items of the array `value`: `value[0]`, `value[1]`, ...

items.name: switch
items.signature: List(Code.Key), U64, U64, List(Code.Tree), Env -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A branch: a `match` on a union, a test of an optional value, a `Bool`
test, or a test of a value against literals (a guard arrives as one).

items.name: branch
items.signature: List(Code.Key), List({ key : Code.Key, tree : Code.Tree }), Code.Tree, (Str -> Try(Str, Ql.Error)), Env -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)
items.docs: The branch itself, when it is not an equality of two optional fields.

items.name: chain
items.signature: List({ test : Str, value : Str }), [Free, Fixed] -> Binding
items.docs:
`IF .. THEN .. ELSE IF .. ELSE .. END`, from arms whose tests exclude
one another. The `ELSE` value is the one most arms give (the last such
arm on a tie), and every arm that gives it needs no test. With `Fixed`,
the last arm is the `ELSE`, because it is the `Default` of a literal
test and has no test of its own.

items.name: presence_equality
items.docs:
The shape the reifier gives `==` on two optional fields: a presence
switch on the first value, and in each arm a presence switch on the
second. Both absent is `true`, one absent is `false`, and both present
compare the two payloads. `!=` has the arms inverted, with `not` around
the comparison. SurrealDB reads an absent field as NONE and `NONE = NONE`
is true, so the comparison of the two values alone answers all four
cases. This gives that comparison, which is the tree of the last arm.
Any other switch is not this shape.

items.name: presence_of
items.signature: Code.Tree -> Try({ node : U32, absent : Code.Tree, present : Code.Tree }, [NotPresenceEquality])
items.docs: A presence switch on a kept node, as the node and its two arms.

items.name: presence_parts
items.signature: List(Code.Key), List(Code.Tree) -> Try({ node : U32, absent : Code.Tree, present : Code.Tree }, [NotPresenceEquality])

items.name: single
items.docs: A region that only delivers one value is that value.

items.name: prim
items.signature: Call, List(Code.Tree), Code.Ty, Env -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A call of a primitive, in the form its id has (`Translate.form`). The
owner and the method of the call name it in a refusal only.

items.name: rendered
items.docs:
The text an extension rendered, at the type of the call. It is taken
as one operand: an extension that writes an operator puts the
parentheses around it.

items.name: sorted
items.signature: Str, List(Code.Evidence), List(Code.Tree), Env -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
`List.sort` and `List.sort_reversed` over items whose Roc order is the order that `array::sort` gives:
the whole numbers and `Dec` by value. The evidence says which `order_relative_to` the sort uses: a type that
writes its own order has a `Row` there, and any order other than a builtin integer's or `Dec`'s is refused.

items.name: table_of
items.docs: A table by its literal name.

items.name: builtin
items.signature: Str, Str, List(Code.Tree), Env -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)

items.name: moments
items.signature: Code.Tree, Code.Tree, Env -> Try([Moments({ left : Str, right : Str }), Texts], Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The operands of an equality where one text is the text of a datetime. The datetimes are compared,
because SurrealDB prints a fraction with 3, 6 or 9 digits and Roc does not. The other text must be a literal.

items.name: library
items.signature: Form, Str, List(Code.Tree), Code.Ty, Env -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A function of `Surreal.Text`, `Hash`, `Array`, `Time`, `Math`, `Rand` or `Geo`, in the
form `Surreal.library` gives its id. `name` names the call in a refusal.

items.name: call
items.docs: A call to a SurrealQL function: `name(a, b)`.

items.name: blank
items.docs: The characters that Roc's `Str.trim` removes, as a SurrealQL regex class.

items.name: ascii_case
items.docs:
The text with the letters from `low` to `high` changed by a SurrealQL
function. It works per character, because `string::uppercase` also
changes the letters outside ASCII, and Roc does not.

items.name: str_lit
items.docs: The text of a string literal, when the tree is one.

items.name: is_nonzero
items.docs: Whether a tree is an integer literal other than zero.

items.name: float_note
items.docs: What a float operation differs in, for a refusal.

items.name: int_try
items.docs:
A conversion `to_<int>_try` of an integer: `NONE` when the value is
outside the range of the target. A value of a SurrealDB int is always
inside the range that has no bound.

items.name: int_range
items.docs:
The bounds of an integer type by its Roc name. A bound is empty when
no value of a SurrealDB int is beyond it.

items.name: list_at
items.docs: The list a list operation runs over, as the start of a method chain.

items.name: list_parts
items.signature: Code.Tree, Env -> Try({ at : Str, items : Items }, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The same, with whether its elements are values, or record ids that a
read traverses: the edges of a relation, or the rows of a table.

items.name: plain_list
items.docs:
A list of values. The edges of a relation and the rows of a table are
record ids, so an operation that gives one element or a new list
refuses them.

items.name: count
items.docs:
`len`: over a group's rows `count()`, or `count(f)` after `keep_if(f)`;
over a list `.len()`.

items.name: sum
items.docs:
`sum`: `map(f).sum()` over a group's rows is `math::sum(f)`, and over a
list `math::sum` of the list.

items.name: aggregate_arg
items.docs:
An aggregate function of a list: over a group's rows `fn(f)` for
`map(f)`, and over a list `fn` of the list. A view refuses
`math::median` over a group's rows (verified).

items.name: aggregate_list
items.signature: Code.Tree, Env -> Try({ text : Str, grouped : Bool }, Ql.Error)
items.docs: The text of the list of an aggregate, and whether it is a group's rows.

items.name: over_group
items.signature: U32, List(Code.Tree), Binding, Env -> Try(Str, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A closure over a group's rows: its parameter is the row the group
aggregates, so `|o| o.total` is `total`.

items.name: lambda
items.signature: Code.Tree, Code.Tree, Str, Env -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A list operation with a closure: `xs.any(|$v1| ..)`. The closure's row
is expanded with its captured values and its element bound to `$vN`,
where `N` is the row's id, so a nested closure never shadows its
parent's variable.

items.name: map_ok
items.docs:
`t.map_ok(f)` on a value that may be NONE: NONE stays NONE, and any
other value is the closure's result.

items.name: expand
items.docs:
A call to one of the application's own functions, expanded with its
parameters bound to what the arguments stand for.

items.name: numeral_text
items.docs:
The exact decimal text of a numeral: the sign, the digits before the
point, and the digits after it, as many as the source wrote. With the
`dec` suffix SurrealQL reads it as a decimal.

items.name: decimal_digits
items.docs:
The decimal digits of a number given in base-256 digits, most
significant first.

items.name: key_compare
items.signature: Code.Tree, Code.Tree, Str, Env -> Try([Keyed(Binding), Plain], Ql.Error)
items.docs:
`==` or `!=` between the key of the row a statement reads and a
value given to the statement (a text literal, a field of the
parameter record, a captured value), in either order, as a
comparison of the record id: `v.id == "tia"` is `id = vet:⟨tia⟩`,
and `v.id == p.key` is `id = type::record('vet', $key)`. It means
the same as `record::id(id) = 'tia'`, as every record of the table
`vet` has the table `vet`, and `type::record` keeps a text key a
text (verified: `type::record('vet', '123')` is `vet:⟨123⟩`, not
`vet:123`). A `SELECT` reads the one record for it and scans the
table for `record::id(id)` (`EXPLAIN`: `RecordIdScan`, `DynamicScan`).

items.name: binary
items.signature: Str, Str, Code.Tree, Code.Tree, Env -> Try(Binding, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
A two-operand builtin as its SurrealQL operator. The normal form puts
an integer literal first in a comparison (`3 < qty`); a comparison
whose left operand is the only literal is written the other way round,
with the mirrored operator.

items.name: is_literal
items.docs:
Whether a tree is a constant: a literal, or a record, list or nominal
of them, such as an `Id` or a `Datetime` written in.

items.name: operator
items.docs:
The SurrealQL operator of a builtin's method. SurrealDB's `/` between
ints truncates toward zero and its `%` follows the dividend, as Roc's
`//` and `%` on integers do.

items.name: Kind
items.signature: [Normal, Relation({ from : Str, to : Str }), View(Try(Str, Ql.Error))]
items.docs:
A normal table, an edge table with the names of the tables its ends
point at, or a view: a table that SurrealDB keeps from a grouped query,
with the text of that query.
items.head: Kind

items.name: Source
items.signature: { name : Str, row_ty : Code.Ty, kind : Types.Kind }
items.docs: A table the schema lists. A link finds its target table here.
items.head: Source

items.name: Field
items.signature: { name : Str, ty : Code.Ty, presence : [Required, Optional, Default(Code.Value), DefaultComputed] }
items.docs:
One field of a record type, as `Code.Ty` describes it. A field with a
`??` default is `Default(value)` when the default is a literal, and
`DefaultComputed` when it is not.
items.head: Field

items.name: FieldDef
items.signature: { path : Str, top : Str, ty : Str, asserts : List(Str), defaults : List({ ty : Code.Ty, value : Code.Value }) }
items.docs:
One `DEFINE FIELD`. `path` is spelled for SurrealQL (`items[*].product`)
and `top` is its first part. `asserts` are conditions over `$value`,
each safe to join with `AND`. `defaults` holds the `??` default of the
field's type, if any, with the type it has: `Schema` writes it as the
`DEFAULT` of the field.
items.head: FieldDef

items.name: Shape
items.signature: [Root, RootOptional, RootList, InObject, InList, InUnionArm({ tag : Str })]
items.docs: Where a link sits. `elements` is True when the site is a `List` of links.
items.head: Shape

items.name: LinkSite
items.signature: { path : Str, top : Str, target : Code.Ty, is_id : Bool, linked : Bool, required : Bool, shape : Types.Shape, elements : Bool, lists : U64 }
items.docs:
A `Link` or an `Id` at any depth. `target` is the row type it points
at; `table_for` turns it into a table. `required` is True when no
optional field, list or union arm is on the way to it.
`linked` is True for a `Linked` of a read row, and `lists` counts
the lists on the way, the list of a `List(Link(r))` too.
items.head: LinkSite

items.name: Nominal
items.signature: [Link, Id, Datetime, Duration, DbFn, TimeKey, Geometry(Str), Linked, Out, In, Try, Bool, Other]
items.docs:
Every nominal type the translator and the schema treat apart, by the
name a `Code.Ty.Named` gives it. This is the one place that compares
those names: `Named` carries no type id (a limit of the reifier today),
so a nominal is known by its name only, and another package's nominal
of the same name would be taken for it. A call is known by its id
(`Translate.Form`), and an opaque type by its `Code.TypeId`.
`Geometry` holds the SurrealDB type of a geometry type of `Surreal`.
items.head: Nominal

items.name: is_point
items.docs: Whether a nominal is a point: SurrealDB reads its `lon` and `lat`.

items.name: user_named
items.docs:
A user nominal is read through to its backing. `Surreal.*` and
`Builtin.*` types are not.

items.name: link_name
items.docs:
The names that a `Recursive` in a described type refers back with,
and that `row_of` and `unfold` take.

items.name: geometry_type
items.docs: The SurrealDB type of a geometry type of `Surreal`.

items.name: check_read
items.docs:
A read row of `table` against its stored row in the registry. They
agree when they have the same fields with the same presence, a
`Linked(r)` stands where the stored row has a `Link` to the row that
`r` agrees with, and every other type is equal. A field
`name : Out(e)` or `name : In(e)` is not stored: `name` is an edge
table that starts (`Out`) or ends (`In`) at `table`, and `e` agrees
with its row.

A read row may hold a `Linked` of itself (`OwnerRead := { ..,
referred_by ?: Linked(OwnerRead) }`). The description gives the
inner one as `Recursive("Surreal.Linked")`, so the comparison is
coinductive: `seen` holds the pairs of a `Linked` and a stored type
that are on the way here, and a pair that is on the way agrees.

items.name: edge_list
items.signature: Code.Ty -> Try({ edge : Code.Ty, end : [From, To] }, [NotEdges])
items.docs: The edge row and the end of the row of an `Out(e)` or an `In(e)`.

items.name: agree_fields
items.signature: Str, List(Types.Field), List(Types.Field), Str, Types.Registry, List(Str) -> Try({}, Ql.Error)

items.name: agree
items.signature: Str, Code.Ty, Code.Ty, Str, Types.Registry, List(Str) -> Try({}, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
One type of a read row against the stored type at the same path.
A `Linked` opens its row with each `Recursive("Surreal.Linked")`
that refers to it in its place (`Types.unfold`). So the walk meets
the same `Linked` again one hop down, and stops there: its pair
with the stored type is in `seen`.

items.name: open
items.docs:
`unwrap` that keeps the meaning of a `Recursive` in the backing: a
nominal row that links to itself, `Owner := { .., referred_by ?:
Link(Owner) }`, holds `Recursive("Owner")`, and the backing has
`Owner` in its place (`Types.unfold`). A walk that compares types
reads it, and stops where the two sides have the same `key`.

items.name: site_of
items.signature: Code.Ty -> Try({ target : Code.Ty, is_id : Bool }, [NotASite])
items.docs:
The row type a `Link` or an `Id` points at, or `Err` for any other type.
A link to a nominal row that links back, `Link(Owner)` with
`referred_by ?: Link(Owner)`, holds `Recursive("Surreal.Link")` in its
row. The target has that link in its place (`Types.unfold`), so a read
of the target sees the same type as a read of the link.

items.name: row_of
items.docs:
The row type of a `Link(row)`, a `Linked(row)` or an `Id(row)` named
`name`: its one type argument.

items.name: unfold
items.docs:
`ty` with each `Recursive(name)` that refers to `whole`, a
`Named(name, ..)`, in its place. A `Recursive` refers to the nearest
`Named` of its name that holds it, so one inside another `Named` of
that name stays.

items.name: key
items.docs:
A name for a row type that is equal for the same type however it was
reached. A nominal is its name: its body shows a link back to itself
differently from each side, so bodies are not compared. A `Link`, a
`Linked` and an `Id` are the key of their row, their type argument.

items.name: table_for
items.docs:
The table that holds rows of this type. Two tables with an equal row
type make a link to it ambiguous, so that is a `BadSchema`.

items.name: check_registry
items.docs: Tables must have different names and different row types.

items.name: check_table
items.docs:
The rules a table must meet, each a `BadSchema` that names the field:
`id : Str` or `id : TimeKey(s)`, the two ends of an edge, no field named
`kind` in a union arm record, no integer wider than `I64`, and only
types SurrealDB has.

items.name: scan_field
items.docs:
A field and its type against the rules. A `??` default that is not
a literal is `DefaultComputed`: the type does not carry its value, so
the schema cannot give it to the database.

items.name: check_end
items.signature: Str, Str, Str, List(Types.Field), Types.Registry -> Try({}, Ql.Error)
items.docs:
An end of an edge is a required `Link` to a row of the table the end
names. The link's row type finds its table in the registry.

items.name: scan
items.docs: One field type, and everything in it, against the rules.

items.name: skipped
items.docs:
Fields with no definition of their own: the record key, and an edge's
two ends. A view has no field definitions at all.

items.name: key_type
items.signature: Str, List(Types.Field), Types.Registry -> Try([Text, Typed(Str)], Ql.Error)
items.docs:
The `TYPE` of the record key, when it is not a text: `[series, datetime]`
for `id : TimeKey(s)`. The series has the type of a field of its Roc
type, and holds no `Link`: a key has no delete policy. A key may have
a literal default (`id : Str ?? "main"`): a create that leaves the key
out gets it, as SurrealDB does for a `DEFAULT` on `id`.

items.name: series_of
items.docs: `TimeKey(s)` holds its series in `series : s`.

items.name: dot
items.docs: A path part after a dot.

items.name: payload_at
items.docs: Payload `i` of an arm with several payloads: `pay.value[1]`.

items.name: int_range
items.signature: Code.Ty -> Try({ lo : I64, hi : I64 }, [NotRanged])
items.docs: The range of a narrow Roc integer, which SurrealDB's `int` does not hold.

items.name: surreal_type
items.docs:
The `TYPE` of a field. A record is `object` and a list of records is
`array<object>`: their fields get their own definitions.

items.name: inline_type
items.docs: A type written out in full, as inside a union arm or an array.

items.name: union_type
items.signature: List({ name : Str, payloads : List(Code.Ty) }), Types.Registry -> Try(Str, Ql.Error)
items.docs: `"A" | { kind: "B", x: X } | { kind: "C", value: Y } | { kind: "D", value: [Y, Z] }`

items.name: constraints
items.docs:
Conditions a value of this type must meet beyond its `TYPE`, over the
expression `subject`. `depth` numbers the closure variables of lists.
Each is safe to join with `AND`. SurrealDB stores a geometry with a
coordinate out of range, so a geometry asserts `geo::is_valid`.

items.name: field_defs
items.docs:
The `DEFINE FIELD` list of a table, parents before children, in name
order. `id` is the record key, and the `from` and `to` of an edge are
SurrealDB's `in` and `out`, so none of the three is defined. A key of a
time series is the exception: its `TYPE` comes first.

items.name: defs_of
items.signature: Str, Str, Types.Field, Types.Registry -> Try(List(Types.FieldDef), Ql.Error)

items.name: leaf
items.signature: Str, Str, Code.Ty, Bool, List({ ty : Code.Ty, value : Code.Value }), Types.Registry -> Try(List(Types.FieldDef), Ql.Error)

items.name: key_check
items.docs:
Elements of an `array<object>` may carry extra keys, so the keys are
checked by a generated condition.

items.name: link_sites
items.docs:
Every `Link` and `Id` in a row type, at any depth, in name order. A
`Link` or `Id` is not entered: it is another table's row. The `from`
and `to` of an edge row are listed like any other link, though they
are SurrealDB's `in` and `out`.

items.name: whole_reads
items.signature: Code.Ty, Str, U64, (Str -> Str), List(Str) -> List({ path : Str, target : Code.Ty, lists : U64 })
items.docs:
The `Linked` rows that a whole value of type `ty` at `path` reads,
under `lists` lists: each `Linked` in it, at any depth, and after each
the `Linked` rows of its own row. A `Link` and an `Id` in it are
record ids. The `target` of each is its row type, whose table
`lookup` finds. A read row that holds a `Linked` of itself has no end,
so a `Linked` of a row in `entered`, by key, is not read again: the
translator refuses that whole row. `spell` spells a field of the row
at `""`, `in` and `out` for the ends of an edge. A live query watches
the table of each (`Translate.whole`, `Selected.live`).

items.name: sites_of
items.docs: The sites of a row type. With `reads`, a `Linked` is a site too.

items.name: Walk
items.signature: { path : Str, top : Str, optional : Bool, nested : Bool, in_list : Bool, tag : Str, reads : Bool, lists : U64 }
items.head: Walk

items.name: site_in
items.signature: Code.Ty, Bool -> Try({ target : Code.Ty, is_id : Bool, linked : Bool }, [NotASite])
items.docs:
A `Link` or an `Id`, and with `reads` a `Linked`, which points at
its row, its type argument, as a `Link` does.

items.name: site
items.signature: Types.Walk, { target : Code.Ty, is_id : Bool, linked : Bool }, Bool -> Types.LinkSite
